Entering the Chamber of Fragrance and Light, Upper Collection
Treatise on the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World
Origin

The Treatise on the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World, existed of old. It was made by an ancient worthy who was greatly and thoroughly awakened, who knew and saw for himself, who held fast to the Buddha’s name alone, cut off delusion and personally realized it; and who then, wishing to repay the Buddha’s grace, rode the wheel of great vows to guide all the deluded universally, so that they might together enter the samadhi fruit-sea and go straight to the other shore of the Land of Bliss. Every word and every letter of it flows from nothing other than the samadhi sea. It may be said to have merit firmer than the kalpa-stone and a value surpassing the mani jewel. Its words are profound, its facts and principles subtle; it penetrates thoroughly, perfectly clear, illumining every hidden place. Like the sun at midday, its light embraces the four continents; unprecedented and unrepeated, without peer. It has benefited countless people, and praise cannot exhaust it. Down to the present it has been revered as a supreme treasure. But what kind of creature am I, that I do not fear my transgression, and dare to confound the ordinary with the sage by usurping its name and writing again? Lightly to take an ordinary being’s knowledge and views and presumptuously fathom the secret cultivation of sages and worthies — thinking it over alone, my offense admits no pardon. I shall now lay bare my foolish feelings as follows, and before the worthies past and present openly confess. This treatise of mine has a certain origin. Before I left home I read little of the poets and books and knew little of the brush; and though after leaving home I studied, again, because I was born in an age of decline and dwelt in a remote region, I seldom met a lofty person to draw near to and cultivate with. Add to this that my good roots are shallow and my power of wisdom slight. Often reading the writings of the ancient worthies, I repeatedly heaved sighs before the high cliff; cowed by the profundity of their words and the subtlety of their facts and principles, unable to grasp them, I was overcome with shame. Though I aroused the mind for Chan and grasped a little, a half-knowledge still could not accomplish the matter — like a firefly trying to burn Mount Sumeru. It is what is called: the principle and the nature, though clear, are hard to penetrate in fact. In the spring of the tenth year of the Republic I first went with my fellow student, the Dharma Master Desen, to Putuo to pay respects to Master Yinguang and respectfully receive his instruction, which was to let go of Chan and devote himself to Buddha-recitation. Not long after, I took my leave, and afterwards went to Tiantai and Jiuhua to offer incense in various places. In the seventh month we returned together to Meijiang, and the next year I dwelt on Baizhang Mountain. Each day I read the Pure Land scriptures and treatises and also held the sacred name of Amitabha. I feel that from then to now I have gradually come to grasp thoroughly the facts and principles, the provisional and the real, of the Pure Land Dharma-gate, with few doubts remaining. Yet I am ashamed that, drifting and careless, I did not notice old age arriving. With my trifling, scattered practice, I fear it will be hard to move the Buddha to welcome me. Therefore I resolved to enter retreat and seek single-mindedness. Who would have thought that after entering the retreat my false thoughts still flowed on as before? Fortunately I feel that the path of principle within it is more familiar than in earlier years. Like the blind men feeling the elephant, though I have not personally known and seen it, I roughly know what its general shape is like. Often in the mind of Buddha-recitation I silently composed a verse: “Thought after thought enter the Buddha-fruit awakening; mind after mind dwell in the Buddha’s right samadhi. Hold fast to the sacred name of Amitabha; at death be welcomed by the Buddha.” Making use of this contemplation, I find it very effective. So I jotted it down as it came, and recently it has grown into a passage on the essentials of Buddha-recitation, with rather deep significance. Because it could not benefit all, I did not dare bring it out to the world; I only enjoyed reading it myself, using it as a guide. Then I reflected again: the Dharma-gate of Buddha-recitation originally gathers all three capacities and receives the whole of the nine realms. It has fact and it has principle; it can be shallow and it can be deep. To expound it freely, why insist on one way? So I suddenly aroused a great resolve and earnestly prayed for the Buddha’s power to be added to me, vowing that this clumsy treatise might be offered universally to my fellows. From then on I wrote again, and without noticing it became a finished work. Considering the meaning of the treatise, it should be named the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World. Compared with the work of the ancient worthy, though the name is not different, in truth we are as far apart as heaven and the abyss. But among my fellows of the age of decline, shallow in good roots, slight in the power of wisdom, unskilled with the brush, and fond of the plain and direct, those like me are many. This clumsy treatise of mine suits the occasion well. If they will arouse the mind to open it and read it with pleasure, each will gain a little something. Within it there is fact and principle, the shallow and the deep; each according to his capacity reaps benefit, and no one’s effort is vainly spent. It is like the sea receiving a hundred rivers: all alike are gathered in and received. Why? Because although Amitabha’s fruit-sea is deep, sentient beings can enter it by utmost sincerity. If we are willing to recite the Buddha with utmost sincerity, all of us can turn the false back to the true, like rivers entering the sea, entering gradually and deeply. After long and thorough familiarization, without our noticing, the true and the false accord, and mind and Buddha are one suchness. From there, advancing further in vigor and cultivating by perfume-drenching in accord with the Dharma, until the work becomes one piece, naturally one neither goes out nor comes in. Thought after thought one dwells at ease in right samadhi; mind after mind one accords with the real mark. Only then does one know that though Ultimate Bliss is far away, it is originally within one’s own present single thought, the great awakening real mind, not a hair’s breadth beyond. Relying on the Buddha’s vast vow-power and his compassionate welcome, what fear is there of not going? What worry of not being born? Straight on until the Saha retribution is exhausted, one will surely be welcomed by our Buddha, just as the full moon comes to the pool, appearing naturally without our noticing. Sustained by the Buddha’s subtle spiritual power, in a moment one arrives in the lotus land. And when the flower opens and one sees the Buddha, one awakens at once to the real mark. From there, advancing gradually, one swiftly realizes the supreme Buddha-fruit. Because it has such inconceivable, surpassing benefits, it is called the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World. This jewel king of samadhi is truly rarely met in a thousand lives, hard to encounter in ten thousand kalpas. I universally vow that my fellows of the ten directions may each arouse the mind to cultivate it. You should know that the benefits above are the portion of everyone, to be obtained by each and all. May all be filled with great joy and together receive wondrous bliss. I have here specially recounted its origin to inform my fellows of the ten directions. Should a reader of this treatise, not disdaining to read it because it was written by an ordinary being heavy with karmic hindrances, further pity my foolish sincerity and ponder it carefully, cultivating by perfume-drenching in accord with it, then together we shall enter the fruit-sea. And I shall join my palms to him and praise him, saying: Excellent! You are my true lotus friend. Now we see and walk together; at the end of life we return together to the Land of Bliss; together we serve the Supreme Vow King, together we verify the supreme Buddha-fruit. Then this clumsy treatise, though it cannot stand beside the ancients’ or serve the same function, may still be called effort not vainly spent — and my hope is fulfilled.
General Discussion: Outline of the Whole

The general title of this clumsy treatise takes the Buddha-fruit as its special school. What is the Buddha-fruit? A single phrase of the Buddha’s name is the whole Buddha-fruit. Vast and boundless, its measure the same as the Dharma-realm, it wholly contains the empty space of the ten directions. The name encompasses the virtues; the whole virtue lies in the name. The name itself is the real; the real itself is the name. Name and reality are non-dual, substance and function one suchness; therefore it is named the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World. This jewel king of samadhi is like a mani jewel, complete in the three great meanings of substance, mark, and function. What are the three meanings? First, the one true alone revealed, emptiness and form perfectly fused, as substance [the middle truth]. Second, pure, clear, and penetrating, with nothing whatsoever obtained, as mark [the true truth]. Third, all virtues together manifest, benefiting without end, as function [the conventional truth]. These three meanings match the three truths. It is what is called: with the middle truth to govern all dharmas, with the true truth to efface all dharmas, with the conventional truth to establish all dharmas. In sum: the Tathagata’s three truths, when a single call of the Buddha’s name is raised, are complete in the very body. If one who recites the Buddha can, mind after mind, penetrate them and understand the perfect fusion, then these three truths match the three contemplations. One need only turn the light around directly, and the practitioner’s present single thought is complete in the very body. It is what is called: the mind that recites is the one-mind three contemplations; the Buddha recited is the one-object three truths. The three contemplations and the three truths correspond in meaning. When the contemplation of the provisional appears in the practitioner, it matches the Tathagata’s conventional truth. When the contemplation of emptiness appears, it matches the Tathagata’s true truth. When the contemplation of the middle appears, it matches the Tathagata’s middle truth. Whenever a practitioner’s single thought corresponds with the Buddha-fruit, it never goes beyond these three meanings. When such contemplation has become familiar, without his noticing the subject and object merge, a single thought accords, and mind and Buddha are one suchness. At that moment the jewel king of samadhi stands alone revealed, perfectly manifest; the light of wisdom penetrates everywhere and fills the ten directions. What has been set out above all belongs to the general meaning. Within this general meaning, two meanings and ten sections are further distinguished to clarify the particular meaning. What are the two meanings? First, the meaning of non-awakening. It refers to those who do not recite the Buddha: thought after thought they are deluded as to the true and chase the false, turning from awakening and joining with dust. Though they are within Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea, they are wholly deluded, and do not understand how to turn the false back to the true and turn from dust to accord with awakening; hence it is called non-awakening. Second, the meaning of awakening. It refers to those who recite the Buddha: thought after thought they turn the false back to the true and turn from dust to accord with awakening. It is what is called: a single call of the Buddha’s name is the whole of Amitabha’s fruit-awakening. The fruit-awakening that Amitabha has verified is the original awakening that sentient beings have lost. If one is willing to recite the Buddha with utmost sincerity, thought after thought penetrating Amitabha’s fruit-awakening and secretly, invisibly according with one’s own original awakening, then though now one is not awakened, on arriving in the West one will at last attain full awakening; hence it is called the meaning of awakening. What are the ten sections? First, clarifying the essential purpose: a single call of the Buddha’s name is the whole Buddha-fruit, and the beings of the nine realms are all gathered in without exception. Second, revealing the real mark: a single call of the Buddha’s name is true and perfectly fused; sages and ordinary beings share one source, beings and Buddhas are one body. Third, distinguishing the true and the false: a single call of the Buddha’s name — purity and defilement are each distinct; Amitabha and sentient beings are as far apart as heaven and earth. Fourth, seeing through blindness and confusion: a single call of the Buddha’s name — let not our fellows be deluded, passing from delusion into delusion and undergoing suffering in turn. Fifth, turning from delusion to awakening: a single call of the Buddha’s name — awaken at once right here; passing from awakening into awakening, one attains ultimate bliss. Sixth, right cause and right fruit: a single call of the Buddha’s name is the right cause of the Buddha-fruit; if one does not realize it in this life, one will surely realize it in the Land of Peace and Nurture. Seventh, comparing the merit and virtue: a single call of the Buddha’s name is the jewel king that emerges from the world; the jewel kings of the world cannot compare with it. Eighth, reconciling the meaning with the sutra: the one Amitabha Sutra is most concise and most perfect, fusing fact and principle, complete in all ten thousand virtues. Ninth, beseeching the Buddha’s attestation: I vow that this clumsy treatise may be offered universally to my fellows, and with this good root dedicated to the Pure Land. Tenth, making vows to circulate it: I vow that to the end of the future, dividing my body into dust-mote lands, I may use this jewel king to benefit and save sentient beings. Such are the two meanings and ten sections, outlined briefly. Their detailed meanings are set out below.
1. Clarifying the Essential Purpose

The Buddha-recitation samadhi, the jewel king that emerges from the world: from ancient times to the present, the patriarchs of every generation have all praised it with one voice and proclaimed it with one mouth. Teaching and capacity accord; it is surpassing beyond compare. It reaches the top [up to equal-enlightenment bodhisattvas] and reaches the bottom [down to birds and beasts]. It is most sudden [no beginning in the former limit, no end in the latter] and most perfect [containing the nine realms, embracing the ten directions]. The great see the great [one phrase of the vast name is the whole of Amitabha’s fruit-awakening]; the small see the small [the four-character name, the six-character name]. The wise speak of wisdom [every phrase Amitabha, concentration and wisdom perfectly clear]; the foolish speak of folly [counting beads, ten thousand or twenty thousand]. Those of provisional capacity follow the provisional [calling the Buddha’s name with the mouth, taking the auspicious marks as the mind’s object]; those of real capacity follow the real [calling the Buddha’s name with the mouth, contemplating the real mark with the mind]. The shallow enter shallowly [reciting aloud or silently, gathering the mind and listening intently]; the deep enter deeply [neither going out nor coming in, dwelling at ease in right samadhi]. Even to cutting off entirely the coarse afflictions of view and thought [semblance samadhi], or partially breaking through subtle ignorance [partial-verification samadhi] — though each differs from the others, every one of them is received as one body by Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea and by his compassionate vow-power [the samadhi fruit-sea is the Tathagata’s Dharmakaya receiving them; the compassionate vow-power is the Tathagata’s spiritual power receiving them]. Hence it is said: the three capacities are universally gathered, the nine realms wholly received. All are made, when this life’s retribution ends, to leave the Saha world and return together to Ultimate Bliss. From then on they never retreat, until ignorance is perfectly broken and the Buddha-fruit is perfected [ultimate samadhi]. So direct, so stable, so universal a deliverance through expedient means. It does not require many lives; in one life one may arrive. Never again retreating, straight to the Buddha’s rank. Such an inconceivable, surpassing, and special Dharma-gate may be called the possession of the Pure Land school alone and of no other school. Were the Buddhas of the ten directions all to put forth the broad and long tongue and praise it to the end of kalpas, praise could not exhaust it. Yet people of the world do not examine it, but regard it as commonplace, pay it no mind, or even slander it. It is like a mani jewel fallen into the mud: people of the world do not recognize it, take it for rubble, and trample it at will. Is this not a great pity?
2. Revealing the Real Mark

Now I provisionally divide into two meanings and set them out, so that this jewel king of samadhi may stand alone revealed, perfectly manifest, giving forth a great light that shines universally upon the Dharma-realm. May all sentient beings, according to what they seek, each have their wish fulfilled, all be filled with great joy, and together obtain wondrous bliss. Even those who merely touch or handle it, see it or hear of it and rejoice — may they soon escape the wheel of suffering and all obtain wondrous bliss, on to the future without end. What are the two meanings? First, the meaning of non-awakening, spoken with reference to those who do not recite the Buddha. Second, the meaning of awakening, spoken with reference to those who do recite the Buddha. I shall first take up the meaning of non-awakening, setting out several kinds below. What is non-awakening? Before Amitabha Buddha became a Buddha, when he first was a wheel-turning king, he made forty-eight great vows before the Buddha Lokesvararaja. Then, through kalpas as many as dust motes, he widely cultivated pure practices and adorned himself with ten thousand virtues, accomplishing the four kinds of Pure Land and welcoming and guiding the beings of the nine realms. He attained the supreme samadhi, the ultimate Buddha-fruit, true and perfectly fused, filling the Dharma-realm, pure and wondrously bright, beyond all thought and speech. Every place and every region it pervades without exception. All the dependent and proper retribution, form and mind, of the ten directions — whether form or emptiness, defiled or pure — alike receive the vast and boundless power of reception of Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea; all are wholly contained without remainder, sealed with a single seal. Because of right concentration it is named samadhi [in Sanskrit, samadhi; here it means right concentration, also right reception]. Seen with the Buddha’s eye, originally sages and ordinary beings share one source, beings and Buddhas are one body. All sentient beings are none other than the Buddha’s children. Each bears his virtue, each receives his grace. Even the tiniest insects are all within the Tathagata’s real-mark samadhi sea, equally nurtured. With a compassionate mind he regards them all equally, seeing no light or heavy; all shall in the future become Buddhas, and in the end not one is abandoned.
3. Distinguishing the True and the False

Consider earnestly: the Tathagata realized the true, and the whole of the false is the true; hence the samadhi fruit-sea came to be. Sentient beings are deluded as to the true, and the whole of the true becomes the false; hence the suffering wheel of birth and death comes to be. Thus sages and ordinary beings occupy different stations, and beings and Buddhas travel different paths. The Tathagata dwells in and sustains the Land of Bliss and forever enjoys wondrous bliss. Sentient beings turn on the wheel of suffering and constantly undergo intense suffering. Each person receives this seed of false karmic consciousness, and each is born through the coming together of causes and conditions. Leaving the womb one enters the shell again; leaving the shell one enters the womb again. Even to moisture-born and transformation-born, birth after birth without end, transformation after transformation without limit. They give up bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges and cast off bones beyond Mount Sumeru. Down to the present life, though one has obtained a human body, this seed of karmic consciousness still drifts through the three realms with no true dwelling place. False and inverted, it cannot be subdued. It is like a mad elephant without a hook, a restless monkey without its chain: thought after thought racing, mind after mind grasping, greedily staining itself with dust-toil without rest. Though it is within the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea through long and vast kalpas, it does not awaken or know. It does not see the real mark of the Tathagata’s fruit-sea, does not recognize the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration. Like a fish dwelling in water and not knowing water, like a bird flying in the sky and not seeing the sky. Though one meets a good friend who with expedient means urges one, teaching one to recite the Buddha and seek birth in Ultimate Bliss, forever leaving the suffering of birth-and-death and the round of rebirth — alas, being blind and confused, one still does not awaken. Many remain drunk on the Saha world, taking suffering for bliss. Though a surpassing and wondrous land of bliss exists, they will not resolve to seek birth there, and willingly undergo all suffering. Is this not sad?
4. Seeing Through Blindness and Confusion

Now, those of whom it is said that they are still drunk on the Saha world and take suffering for bliss: this is entirely because they do not believe at all. Those who, though a surpassing and wondrous land of bliss exists, will not resolve to seek birth there: this is because their belief, though present, is incomplete. Some half-believe and half-doubt; some believe but do not vow; some vow but do not practice; some practice but not single-mindedly; some covet fame and profit and hope for blessed reward; some seek the miraculous and also practice other paths. Because of such deficiencies and admixtures, they do not resolve to seek birth. For these dull and sluggish folk even the Buddha can do nothing; he can only let down compassion and pity and wait for the time [though all sentient beings are within the Tathagata’s samadhi sea, because they reject Ultimate Bliss and will not seek birth, in the end they gain no benefit]. Therefore through immeasurable kalpas they flow on in birth and death, circling through the six paths like a wheel, down to this day without cease. Now that they have met the Buddha-recitation samadhi, the jewel king that emerges from the world, if they are still blind and confused and will not single-mindedly recite the Buddha and seek birth in Ultimate Bliss, the Buddha will only let down still greater compassion and pity. It is said: though sentient beings do not recite the Buddha, the Buddha is always mindful of sentient beings. Such people who do not recite the Buddha are all drunkards of the world. Because they do not believe and do not practice, though they are within the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea, through a hundred thousand kalpas they never awaken. It is what is called: from delusion into delusion, undergoing suffering in turn. Alas, how painful! These deeply drunken people may still be set aside for the moment. What must urgently be discussed is this: there are, sadly, people of deep past roots who in this life again meet a good friend, hear of Chan and the teachings, draw near and cultivate, and whose mind-nature is clear, so that they seem to be awakened and call themselves wise, mocking Buddha-recitation. Such practitioners, if they do not recite the Buddha and seek birth in Ultimate Bliss and draw near to Amitabha, are in the end not secure. Why? Because ordinary beings of the age of decline are heavy in delusion and karma and weak in self-power. Even meeting a good friend’s guidance and seeming to awaken, they cannot in this life cut off delusion and karma entirely, pass beyond the three realms, and dwell at ease in non-retrogression. In later lives they remain in the Saha world, turning in birth and death. After turning through many lives, they cannot avoid losing their way and falling. If they fall into the three evil paths, then for a hundred kalpas and a thousand lives they will not hear the Buddha’s name. When they may obtain a human body and awaken again is quite uncertain. It is like a person fast asleep: though he is occasionally disturbed by someone and half rouses, because his own strength is exhausted he cannot rouse himself to go out and look around, but leans back on the pillow and sleeps on, while in dreams his karmic consciousness drifts east and west. Though his parents are beside him and his wife and children fill the room, his nearest and dearest, he does not perceive or know them. The ordinary being of shallow awakening is likewise. I have heard it said that arhats have the delusion of leaving the womb and bodhisattvas have the stupor of the intervening shade — how much more the ordinary being of shallow awakening. Therefore one who does not recite the Buddha, even if he seems to awaken, is in the end not secure, cannot avoid falling back, and remains blind and confused; hence all of them are named the meaning of non-awakening.
5. Turning from Delusion to Awakening

What is the meaning of awakening? I now divide it into two: first, the keen are clear and penetrating; second, the middling and dull are secretly in accord. I shall first take up the keen. Those of keen capacity who wish in this life to enter deeply into the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration: while rightly reciting the Buddha, the mouth calls the Buddha’s name and the mind awakens to the real mark. You should know that the real mark is the vast name and the vast name is the real mark. It is what is called: the name encompasses the virtues; the whole virtue lies in the name. The name is the dharani that contains ten thousand virtues, and when one is raised, all are gathered in. It is directly of one body, one time, and one function with the wondrous principle of the real mark, not two, not different. But since I have often heard that the real mark has no gate, by what means shall we now awaken and enter? Let me explain below. One who wishes to awaken to and enter the Tathagata’s wondrous principle of the real mark should first, by way of analogy, think of a dragon dwelling in the sea: the seawater contains it and it has never left. Every place and every region is nothing but seawater. Then let him reflect that we sentient beings are likewise. Through immeasurable kalpas we have constantly dwelt in Amitabha’s samadhi sea; the real mark contains us and we have never left it. Every place and every region is nothing but the real mark. But because we are deluded, we do not awaken or know. It is like a drunkard who is in his own grandfather’s house, wholly contained within it, never having left; yet because his mind is clouded he falsely sees mountain forests and open plains, marketplaces and theaters. Now grieving, now rejoicing, now laughing, now talking, babbling confusedly, “I want to go home.” One who is awake tells him: “You are even now in your own grandfather’s house, dwelling at ease and unmoving; why speak of going home?” We sentient beings are likewise. Through immeasurable kalpas we have constantly been within Amitabha’s samadhi sea, and down to this day have never left it. You should know that today there is no need to enter again. One need only, thought after thought, look back: this present single thought, my false mind of karmic consciousness, is originally within the Tathagata’s pure real-mark sea, neither going out nor coming in, dwelling at ease in right concentration. From now on one should simply still the mind and recite the Buddha, and no longer rush about and drift. Should one rush about and drift again, gather it back at once. When such contemplation has long been familiar, without one’s noticing one penetrates the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark and dwells at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration. It is what is called: with one thought unmoving, one dwells for one thought in the Buddha’s right concentration; with every thought unmoving, one dwells for every thought in the Buddha’s right concentration. Why? The Tathagata’s real-mark right concentration is like the water of the great sea, and our false mind of karmic consciousness is like the waves on the water. One need only, thought after thought, keep utmost sincerity in the mind and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s real-mark fruit-sea, like water dwelling in water, according and perfectly fused. Until the work becomes one piece, naturally one neither goes out nor comes in, neither changes nor moves. This is exactly what is called using the cause to accord with the fruit and borrowing the fruit to perfect the cause. Obtaining a portion of the Buddha’s fragrance, the wondrous fruit will surely appear. If one can long think and contemplate in this way, one will feel the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea gradually becoming clear and gradually appearing before one. Just as it appears, one suddenly feels inside and outside wholly penetrating, the fruit-sea entirely manifest. True and perfectly fused, it fills the Dharma-realm. Every place and every region is nothing but the real mark. And within the substance of the real mark, each and every adornment is complete; and each and every adornment is nothing but the principle-substance of the real mark. It is what is called: one act, two gains; fact and principle at the same time. It is like a mirror’s image or the moon in water, originally neither identical nor apart, neither one nor different. Awakening to this, one knows that substance and function are both manifest and provisional and real are one. Since one can thus awaken mind after mind, one should accept it thought after thought; do not be careless and miss it, losing what will be hard to meet in later lives. When such awakening has long been familiar and one’s acceptance is complete and all-pervading [the whole Dharma-realm, one true real mark], naturally one’s mindfulness is present wherever one is. When a single thought is present, one suddenly feels body and mind unmoving, deeply entering the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark. Not leaving one’s own position, one dwells at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration, according and perfectly fused, pervading the Dharma-realm [the present single thought of consciousness can be the whole Dharma-realm]. This is exactly what is called: with the awakening of the Buddha’s fruit-ground to penetrate my mind of the cause-ground [sealing the mind with the Buddha], and with my mind of the cause-ground to encompass the awakening of the Buddha’s fruit-ground [sealing the Buddha with the mind]. Direct and to the point, the whole completely perfect [mind and Buddha perfectly fused, mind and Buddha one suchness]. Truly pure and subtle, beyond all thought and speech. With this merit one dedicates it to Ultimate Bliss and makes the vow to be reborn: this may be called the provisions for the highest grade. For one can be complete in faith and vows, hold the Buddha’s name, be received by the Buddha, and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea. At the end of life one will certainly be welcomed by the Buddha and reborn in the Land of Bliss. If one attains perfect verification of the ultimate samadhi, one will be born in the Pure Land of Eternally Quiescent Light. If one attains partial verification of the samadhi, one will be born in the Pure Land of Real Reward Adornment. If one attains semblance samadhi, one will be born in the Pure Land of Expedient With-Remainder. Even if the power of one’s cultivation does not reach so far and one does not personally realize it in this life, one’s effort is still not vainly spent. Riding the power of perfuming cultivation of this jewel king of samadhi and relying on the Buddha’s welcome, one will be reborn in the Land of Co-residence, and one’s grade will certainly be high. This is spoken with reference to the keen; the middling and dull are taken up below.
6. Right Cause and Right Fruit

Next, as for those of middling capacity, their awakening is incomplete; those of dull capacity awaken only a little, or not at all. If one cannot grasp the true and wondrous principle above, one may simply devote oneself to practice in fact, suiting one’s own capacity, seeking what is secure and not losing one’s place in the lotus, and that too is enough. Let me now speak in sum. Whether awakened or not, one need only arouse faith, make vows, and earnestly hold the name; and even simple men and women can be made to penetrate the Buddha’s wisdom secretly and accord with the wonder of the Way invisibly. How do we know this? Though simple men and women do not clearly understand the Tathagata’s true and wondrous principle, yet because in reciting the Buddha they keep utmost sincerity in the mind thought after thought, they can turn from dust to accord with awakening and turn the false back to the true. When this is long and thoroughly familiar, without their noticing the true and the false accord and faculties and objects merge with each other. There is only the Buddha-name, clear and distinct, thought following thought in succession, phrase linked to phrase. It communicates closely and accords invisibly with the mind of the Tathagata’s true and wondrous principle. Hence it is said: the keen are clear and penetrating, the middling and dull secretly in accord. And being secretly in accord, each and every one is received as one body by Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea and by his compassionate vow-power. All who recite the Buddha can, in this life, together enter the samadhi. With one thought calling the Buddha, one enters the samadhi for one thought; with every thought calling the Buddha, one enters the samadhi for every thought. It is like water poured into water, whether clear or turbid, naturally in accord. There is only the difference of realm, great or small, bright or dark, provisional or real, shallow or deep, ultimate or not. Therefore the grade each obtains differs also in height and rank. With this merit one dedicates it to Ultimate Bliss and makes the vow to be reborn: this may be called the provisions of the middling and dull. For one can be complete in faith and vows, hold the Buddha’s name, be received by the Buddha, and enter the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea. At the end of life one will certainly be welcomed by the Buddha and reborn in the Land of Bliss. It is like a blind simpleton crossing the sea: once he boards the ship of universal deliverance, though he does not personally know or see what the realm aboard the ship is like, he naturally arrives at the other shore with the others. We who recite the Buddha are likewise. The single phrase Amitabha is the ship of compassion on the sea of suffering. If one can arouse faith, make vows, and earnestly hold the name, one is complete in these three kinds of provisions. Though one does not clearly understand the true and wondrous principle within the Tathagata’s samadhi sea, one naturally arrives with the others at the other shore of the Land of Bliss. The grade obtained will be among the middling and lower of the Land of Co-residence. Compared with the keen, though there is the difference of higher and lower grade and of seeing the Buddha sooner or later, when one reaches the stage of Buddhahood all are equal without difference, together verifying the supreme bodhi. That is, the samadhi fruit-sea above is in each case perfectly complete [the samadhi fruit-sea is another name for bodhi]. Even those of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, birds and beasts and the like, if they meet a good friend’s guidance, can at once arouse faith, make vows, strive earnestly, and call the Buddha’s name. All are received by the Buddha and guided home to the Land of Bliss, attached to the lowest grade [all sentient beings are originally within the samadhi sea of Amitabha, the compassionate father; with a single thought of dedication they are at once received]. When the flower opens and they see the Buddha and hear the Buddha speak the Dharma, they awaken on the spot, and advancing from there all reach the Buddha’s rank. All such as these who recite the Buddha belong to the world-transcending practitioners. For they can in this life enter the Buddha’s samadhi and return together to the path of awakening; when their retribution ends they are reborn in Ultimate Bliss and together ascend to non-retrogression, until the Buddha-fruit is perfected [the single phrase Amitabha is the right cause of the Buddha-fruit] and they arrive together at the ultimate shore of awakening. Therefore those who recite the Buddha, from first to last, do nothing but turn from dust to accord with awakening, until the great perfect awakening; hence all of them are named the meaning of awakening. What was said above — that the jewel king of samadhi is provisionally divided into two meanings — has now been set out. Below I shall again compare the merit of worldly treasures, and only then will one know that the wonder of the Buddha’s name is wonder beyond all thought.
7. Comparing the Merit and Virtue

Now, a single call of the Buddha’s name is the whole Buddha-fruit. Vast and boundless, its measure the same as the Dharma-realm. The name encompasses the virtues; the whole virtue lies in the name. The three bodies and four lands are complete in adornment. Self-benefit and other-benefit are complete as one thinks of them. The whole of fact is principle; the whole of principle is fact. Fact and principle perfectly fused, provisional and real one suchness. One who understands the provisional knows the provisional and draws the provisional back to the real. One who sees the real sees the real, and the provisional itself is the real. It is like a mani jewel, transparent within and without, wholly perfect and bright, originally with nothing whatsoever obtained. Though nothing whatsoever is obtained, it does not prevent the ten thousand appearances from appearing all at once. Though the ten thousand appearances appear all at once, originally nothing whatsoever is obtained. Because it has such inconceivable, subtle benefit, it is called the Buddha-recitation samadhi, the jewel king that emerges from the world. This jewel king of samadhi is beyond all the wondrous treasures of the world. Why? The most precious wondrous treasure in the world is none other than the king of mani jewels, which can well grant whatever one seeks and satisfy everything. Compared with the jewel king of samadhi, not only can one king of mani jewels not match it: were all the kings of mani jewels in the ten directions of the world gathered together in one place, heaped up to the Brahma heaven, all their merit and benefit could not, by counting or simile, match one part, half a part, or even a minute part of the merit and benefit of this jewel king of samadhi. Why? Worldly wondrous treasures can only let one leave suffering and gain bliss temporarily in the world; they cannot cause one to leave the world and be free of ultimate suffering and attain ultimate bliss. Therefore by counting or simile they can never match it. For this jewel king of samadhi, the Buddha-recitation samadhi that emerges from the world, can cause all sentient beings, when this life’s retribution ends, to transcend the turbid world horizontally and enter the lotus land directly. Forever leaving the many sufferings of the Saha world’s six paths, they constantly receive the wondrous bliss of the West’s nine grades. At all times they serve the Compassionate Honored One; step by step they follow the assembly of the sea. Jeweled robes and jade-like food come as one thinks, at the mind’s wish. Wondrous birds proclaim the Dharma; heavenly music resounds in the sky. Jeweled flowers constantly drift down; rare fragrance perfumes all around. Gold is the ground; varied jewels are the pools. The water has eight virtues; the trees are ranged with the seven precious things. Pavilions of many jewels, auspicious and peaceful. Should one wish to go to other regions, one flies at will, swiftly and surely, arriving in a moment. One makes offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions and learns all Dharma-gates. One is complete in the five eyes and six superknowledges, and perfects the three bodies and four wisdoms. One saves boundless sentient beings and receives the prophecy of future Buddhahood. Such ultimate, inconceivable, pure and wondrous bliss shares one lifespan with Amitabha, the World-Honored One, and to the end of the future is enjoyed forever without end. Therefore the Buddhas of the ten directions all praise it and the beings of the nine realms all return to it, like the stars surrounding the North Star, like a hundred rivers flowing east. Truly it is rarely met in a thousand lives, hard to encounter in ten thousand kalpas. That we now meet it is also because we planted the lotus cause in former lives. Now we should cultivate it deeply and richly; do not, we pray, put it off and miss it. Time passes easily; regret is hard to overtake. One stumble leads to a hundred; one falls back again and again. While our strength and health remain, let us all strive at perfuming cultivation. The keen may verify it in this life and accomplish the provisions of the highest grade. The middling and dull cultivate according to their strength and prepare provisions for rebirth. With the end of this retribution as the term, we return together to the Land of Peace and Nurture. So may we always follow the Buddha in learning, swiftly realize the supreme bodhi, and thereby above repay the grace of the Buddhas and below relieve the suffering of the three evil paths. I universally vow that the sentient beings of the nine realms may go together to the lotus land, draw near the Vow King, and together perfect the fruit-sea. The meanings discussed above follow especially the smaller Amitabha Sutra: the one phrase of the vast name, ten thousand virtues perfectly fused, the most surpassing, subtle, inconceivable jewel king of samadhi; and its main purport has been briefly set out. Below I shall again reconcile it with the meaning of the sutra.
8. Reconciling the Meaning with the Sutra

The one Amitabha Sutra belongs in meaning to the Buddha Vehicle. Its words are brief, yet its facts and principles are complete. As for perfect fusion without obstruction and sudden transcendence to the ultimate, it is directly equal to the Avatamsaka and the Lotus. Even equal-enlightenment bodhisattvas have not yet reached its limit and must take one step further. Why? Because it is purely the Amitabha Tathagata, who through kalpas of cultivation and the adornment of ten thousand virtues has perfectly verified the supreme samadhi fruit-sea. This one sutra may be called complete in the three bodies and complete in the four lands. Host and companions interpenetrate; self and other are non-dual. Dependent and proper retribution are perfectly fused; form and mind are one body. The land itself is the body and the body itself is the land. Body and land are non-dual, the real mark one suchness. Seen in this way, is it not equal to the Avatamsaka and the Lotus? As for expedient welcome and guidance, it far surpasses all other sutras. Even simple men and women, those of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, birds and beasts — if they can earnestly recite the Buddha, at the end of life they enter the lotus land; all are received alike, without exception or abandonment. As for security and directness, even one in the lowest grade of the lowest birth has already forever ascended to non-retrogression, and advancing from there reaches the Buddha’s rank. As for ease of practice, it is only one phrase of the vast name, containing ten thousand virtues, which anyone can do. This one phrase of the vast name gathers in all beings of the nine realms, returning them together to Ultimate Bliss and causing them all in the future to become Buddhas one after another. Seen in this way, does it not far surpass all other sutras? Therefore Shakyamuni Tathagata, out of a thorough compassion, for the sake of us ordinary beings of the last age, heavily obstructed, who cannot by our own power know the mind and reach the origin, cut off delusion and verify the truth, poured it all out without concealing a hair. Wishing to fulfill his own heart, he therefore spoke unasked. With bitter words he admonished; with a grandmother’s heart he urged and entrusted. “If there are those who believe, they should make vows, wishing to be born in that land.” Having faith and vows, one should further hold fast to the Buddha’s name, even to single-mindedness. For single-mindedness is deep entry into Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea. And the samadhi fruit-sea is the vast name of ten thousand virtues. Apart from the vast name of ten thousand virtues, where else is there a samadhi fruit-sea? Apart from the samadhi fruit-sea, where else is there a vast name of ten thousand virtues? This one phrase of the vast name is the dharani that encompasses the immeasurable wondrous practices and merits of Amitabha’s causal and fruit grounds. If one wishes to cultivate merit widely, thickly accumulate provisions, adorn the Pure Land, and hope for the highest grade, one may also read the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, the Sutra of the Contemplation of Immeasurable Life, and the great works and grand writings of the patriarchs of the Pure Land school; these I shall not record at length. Let the reader forgive me and not take offense.
9. Beseeching the Buddha’s Attestation

I am further ashamed that, not measuring my own mediocrity and folly, I was for a time presumptuous, and these words occasionally flowed out naturally from the mind of Buddha-recitation. So I jotted them down as they came, and without noticing they gradually grew into a finished work. But having long neglected learning and being unskilled with the brush, though I have written something, my words do not make a composition. Hence these expressions lack elegance and the facts and principles fall short of completeness. Add to this that, with the knowledge and views of an ordinary being heavy with karmic hindrances, I presumptuously fathom the secret cultivation of sages and worthies. All this is because my heart for the Dharma is urgent and my wish to benefit people is earnest; even where there is obscurity or omission, I have had no leisure to attend to it. I respectfully look to lotus friends, monastic and lay, near and far, to love me with compassion and point things out clearly, so that I may correct them — a blessing beyond measure. Further, I offer this rough writing before the Buddha, earnestly praying the Buddhas of the ten directions and Shakyamuni Tathagata to discern and attest it. I respectfully ask the compassionate father Amitabha, who welcomes and guides to the West, to let down his blessing. I bow my head to the great sages and worthies in the assembly of the Land of Bliss, asking them to instruct me in secret. I humbly pray the Lotus Societies of past and present and the patriarchs of every generation to grant guidance from the unseen. Your disciple has reverently composed this clumsy treatise and offers it universally to my fellows of the ten directions, dedicating this small portion of good root to the Ultimate Bliss Pure Land. May my karmic hindrances be wholly dissolved, my wisdom alone shine bright, the lotus platform be long since prepared, the fruit-sea swiftly perfected. May I, when death approaches, know the time in advance. May my body be free of illness and pain, my mind not confused; may all my faculties be joyful and my right mindfulness clear. May I relinquish my retribution in peace, as if entering Chan concentration. May the Buddha’s majestic golden body, dazzling and radiant, come with all the assemblies of sages to welcome me, standing in the air and displaying every auspicious sign — heavenly music by the hundred and thousand, banners and canopies without number — moving sentient beings to arouse the bodhi-mind. At that time may I ride the vajra platform and, sustained by the Buddha’s subtle spiritual power, in a snap of the fingers enter the lotus land. There, when the flower opens and I see the Buddha and hear the Buddha expound the real mark, may I awaken at once to the unproduced and in a moment travel through the ten directions, serving immeasurable Buddhas and learning all Dharma-gates. Complete in the power of the patience of the unproduced, personally receiving the prophecy from all the Buddhas, may they all stroke my head and say with praise: Before long you will be no different from me. Returning then to my native Ultimate Bliss, I will serve the Supreme Compassionate Honored One; without moving my subtle form, I will manifest transformation bodies beyond number, ever acting as the Tathagata’s envoy, teaching and guiding the deluded throughout the ten directions.
10. Making Vows to Circulate It

Again I vow: through this present life’s retribution body and on to the future Buddha-body, I will constantly use this pure and subtle Dharma-gate, the Buddha-recitation samadhi, the jewel king that emerges from the world, to teach and transform immeasurable, countless, inconceivable sentient beings to arouse the bodhi-mind. May I, when I become a Buddha, transform one inconceivable, subtle, well-adorned body into immeasurable, countless, inconceivable subtle, well-adorned bodies, universally appearing in immeasurable, countless, inconceivable worlds of the ten directions, to the end of the future constantly performing the Buddha’s work. Each with one inconceivable, subtle tongue, may I send forth immeasurable, countless, inconceivable subtle sounds, and every sound be complete in immeasurable, countless, inconceivable true and wondrous meanings. With this Buddha-recitation samadhi, the jewel king that emerges from the world, may I expound and teach immeasurable, countless, inconceivable beings of every different kind, guiding them all to return together to the Land of Bliss, draw near the compassionate father Amitabha, and learn the various Dharma-gates. From then on, never retreating until the supreme bodhi is perfected, all equal to Amitabha Buddha without difference. Even merit, lifespan, wisdom, and spiritual power shall likewise be equal without difference. If the vows I have now made are not fulfilled, then though the empty space of the ten directions should come to an end everywhere, these my vows and my cultivation shall never rest. Thought after thought in succession, without interruption; body, speech, and mind, without weariness. Now, wishing with this Buddha-recitation samadhi, the jewel king that emerges from the world, to gather together all the meanings of the whole work, I restate them in a verse:
One Name, Amitabha — no praise can sound its end; ten thousand virtues held, one perfectly fused whole.
All beings who recite return together to the Pure Land; high grade or low, by their own merit each must stand.
Conclusion: Protecting the Right and Rescuing the Biased

When this clumsy treatise was first finished, a visitor asked to read it. Having read it, he said: Reverently reading your lofty discourse, I deeply admire it. It shows our Master’s whole grandmotherly heart earnestly expounding the profound meaning of Buddha-recitation, like opening a treasure house where a hundred treasures all appear. All who have eyes see it; all who have understanding know it. It universally causes everyone joyfully to enter the treasure house and each, according to his own capacity, to choose what is beneficial. Not only is the effort not vainly spent; it may also be called beautiful and good. But since you teach people to recite the Buddha and seek birth in Ultimate Bliss, why do you not take the Pure Land as the school, so that people’s minds take Ultimate Bliss as their object and thus have somewhere to return? The Master takes the Buddha-fruit as the school and leads people to enter deeply into the Buddha-fruit. I do not know whether the two schools, the Pure Land and the Buddha-fruit, are different. The answer: They differ slightly. The visitor said: What is the difference? Pray instruct me. The answer: If one relies on the Sutra of the Sixteen Contemplations and devotes oneself to the contemplations of the Pure Land realm, one should take the Pure Land as the school. Now, relying on the Amitabha Sutra and single-mindedly holding the sacred name of Amitabha’s ten thousand virtues in the hope of attaining single-mindedness, one should take the Buddha-fruit as the school. The visitor said: The Master uses the Buddha’s name to express the Buddha-fruit, but the Buddha’s name is only six characters — how can it be a school? The answer: Have you not seen what Master Chewu says: even a mustard seed or a dust mote can be a school — how much more the fruit-ground Amitabha, the treasury of the Dharma-realm, adorned with ten thousand virtues? Can he alone not be a school? This clumsy treatise, taking the Buddha-fruit as its special school, means exactly this. The visitor said: Since the Buddha-fruit is the school, what after all is the benefit? The answer: This benefit is of two kinds. First, the benefit of the Tathagata, host and companions. Second, the benefit of sentient beings. As for the Tathagata’s benefit, host and companions: it is what is called — a single phrase of the Buddha’s name is the whole Buddha-fruit. The one true alone revealed, ten thousand virtues all manifest. The three bodies perfect, the four lands complete. Host and companions interpenetrating, self and other non-dual. Dependent and proper retribution perfectly fused, form and mind one body. The land itself the body, the body itself the land. Body and land non-dual, the real mark one suchness. Vast and boundless, its measure the same as the Dharma-realm; all that is in the ten directions it contains without exception. As for the benefit of sentient beings: raising a single call of the Buddha’s name directly encompasses the Tathagata’s immeasurable merit and virtue [the cause can encompass the fruit] and wholly gathers in the practitioner’s every wondrous practice [the fruit can gather in the cause]. This is exactly what is called: with the cause encompassing the fruit, and borrowing the fruit to gather in the cause. Cause and fruit gather each other in; beings and Buddhas merge with each other. It can cause the practitioner, without moving body or mind, to enter deeply into the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark [entering the Buddha’s right concentration]. Not leaving his own position, he dwells at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration [dwelling in the Buddha’s right concentration]. Having entered Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea, the Ultimate Bliss Pure Land is right within it. Apart from Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea, where else is there an Ultimate Bliss Pure Land? If one is of the very highest capacity, then striving from here at perfuming cultivation and not retreating to the end of life, one day when the work of pure karma is accomplished, the surpassing realm of Ultimate Bliss may be seen even in this life [in ancient times there were very many such]. It is like a man entering the sea and seeing the dragon palace with his own eyes — what doubt can there be? Even if one does not see it in this life, at the end of life one will certainly see it. Therefore the ancients, at the time of death, could well know the hour in advance, with right mindfulness clear, dying seated or standing, passing peacefully to the West. Heavenly music by the hundred and thousand, banners and canopies without number, the Buddha and the assembly of sages coming through the air to welcome them. That beings with the conditions all saw and heard it came wholly from the power of Amitabha’s fruit-sea right concentration. But such rebirths with the most conspicuous auspicious signs, though they existed in ancient times, were not many even then. Or else those beside them did not see it and only the one being reborn saw it himself; this was the most common. We ordinary beings of the age of decline are heavy in karmic hindrances, shallow in faculties, darkened in knowledge, and slack in practice. Yet if we are only willing to arouse the mind and cultivate, though we do not personally realize it in this life, we still obtain the perfumed portion of the samadhi. Therefore Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva says: like a person steeped in incense whose body bears its fragrance, this is called adorned with Fragrance and Light. You should know that the great being’s profound meaning lies exactly here. Hence the great being says of himself: I, in my original causal ground, by the mind of Buddha-recitation, entered the patience of the unproduced. To say he entered the patience of the unproduced is to say he entered the patience of the real mark. Personally verifying the real mark is called attaining the unproduced. Having attained the unproduced, complete in the power of patience, it is called the patience of the unproduced. To understand it otherwise is to mistake the great being’s profound meaning. Yet even without mistaking it, one has not reached the ultimate. Why? What is called adorned with Fragrance and Light is this: while we are rightly reciting the Buddha, the whole body penetrates the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark and dwells at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration, constantly receiving the Tathagata’s fragrance of immeasurable merit and light of wisdom, perfuming and illumining the whole body. It causes the afflictions and karmic hindrances of our immeasurable kalpas to be extinguished mind after mind, and our merit and wisdom to grow thought after thought. This is what is called: adorning oneself with the Buddha’s adornment and sustaining oneself with the Buddha’s sustaining; hence it is called adorned with Fragrance and Light. It is like black iron cast into a furnace, which in a moment takes on the color of the fire’s light; like white ice thrown into boiling water, which at once becomes one body with the water. These are common worldly things, yet they have such power of fusion. How much more should this subtle spiritual power, the inconceivable world-transcending Buddha-recitation samadhi, fall short of their benefit? The visitor said: The Tathagata’s samadhi spiritual power is inconceivable; your disciple long ago deeply believed and revered it. But the realm of the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea is exceedingly deep. Your disciple is a beginner of shallow learning, foolish and benighted in knowledge, and does not understand principle and nature. How can I enter it? The answer: This was already explained in the treatise above — why did you not notice as you read? Though the realm of the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea is deep, you should know that sentient beings can enter it by a single thought of utmost sincerity. It is what is called: with one thought of utmost sincerity, one enters the samadhi for one thought; with every thought of utmost sincerity, one enters the samadhi for every thought. Why? Because while we are rightly reciting the Buddha and keep utmost sincerity in the mind thought after thought, it can cause us gradually to turn from dust and accord with awakening, to turn the false back to the true; therefore we can enter. If you can now only, in this way, keep utmost sincerity in the mind thought after thought, without needing to understand principle and nature, then when it is long and thoroughly familiar, without your noticing you will penetrate the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration. Having penetrated the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark and dwelling at ease in the Tathagata’s samadhi right concentration, from then on you should simply still the mind and recite the Buddha. Contemplate thought after thought; always let right mindfulness dwell at ease in the real mark, and do not let it drift. Should it drift again, gather it back; the more you practice the more familiar it becomes, entering gradually and deeply. It is like a bee gathering honey, never weary of taking the taste; once it has the taste of honey, it cannot be driven away. We who recite the Buddha are likewise. If one can know the taste of the samadhi’s bliss, one will not let the mind let go of it thought after thought. Again, it is like a child eating candy: the more he eats, the more he wants. At such a time the work of Buddha-recitation accords in some small measure. If from there one can advance further in vigor and cultivate by perfume-drenching in accord with the Dharma, one will surely enter deeply into the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark. Having entered deeply into the Tathagata’s fruit-sea real mark, one accords in a greater measure. One feels of oneself that the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea is vast and boundless, filling the Dharma-realm, penetrating and perfectly clear, fused and unobstructed. One thought is the whole and the whole is one thought. Neither going out nor coming in, one dwells at ease in right concentration. The very body is one suchness, suddenly according with the real mark. This is exactly what is called: contemplate the body as the real mark; so too the Buddha and sentient beings. If one understands this meaning, one knows that mind, Buddha, and sentient beings are three without difference, the same one true real mark [if one wishes to see Amitabha’s true suchness Dharmakaya, one sees it as one wishes]. Though one cannot cut off entirely the coarse afflictions of view and thought, or partially break through subtle ignorance and partially verify the true suchness real mark, one may by this gradually reduce the drifting and set the mind at ease in Buddha-recitation. It is like opening a pool to await the moon: one need only hope that our mind-water is full and the waves of false thought are calmed, that the drifting is reduced and the real mark somewhat accorded, that we recite the Buddha with a settled mind and await the Buddha’s welcome. What fear is there that at death the surpassing realm will not appear and the Buddha will not come to welcome us? Not only does one not lose the right cause of rebirth; one’s grade at birth will be high. Even without any conspicuous auspicious sign for people to see, if one can keep the mind unscattered and right mindfulness clear, be moved by the Buddha’s welcome, and pass peacefully to the West, that too is enough. Because it has such inconceivable, subtle benefit, it takes the Buddha-fruit as the school. You should know that a single phrase of the Buddha’s name is the whole Buddha-fruit; it can be broad or brief, can expand or contract. Broad, it contains the three baskets; brief, it returns altogether to six characters. Expanded, it pervades the ten directions; contracted, it is gathered into a single thought. This is exactly what is called: gathering in all six faculties, pure mindfulness continuing in succession. If one can know this meaning, then, like a fisherman casting his net, what harm if a thousand lines all spread out, when a single pull of the rope gathers them in at once? This is where the wonder of the Buddha’s name lies. The visitor said: A single phrase of the Buddha’s name is the whole Buddha-fruit; sentient beings who call it accord with principle and with capacity. Cause and fruit gather each other in; beings and Buddhas merge with each other. It can be broad or brief, can expand or contract. Having received the Master’s instruction, I find it wondrous to the utmost. But as for holding the name while also cultivating the contemplation of the realm, whether the two agree or not, your disciple does not understand; pray instruct me clearly. The answer: If one wishes also to cultivate the contemplation of the realm, and can awaken to the true realm of quiescent light, then it is of one body, one time, and one function with the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea, not two, not different. Why? Because it is the one true Dharma-realm. For this one true Dharma-realm is the Tathagata’s adorned fruit-sea and the sentient beings’ original-awakening true mind. All the great sages and worthies of old who finely cultivated wondrous contemplation took this original-awakening true mind as their substance. You should know that the original-awakening true mind is the one-mind three contemplations [the very body as the provisional, the empty, and the middle]. Relying on this original-awakening true mind to arouse the cultivation of wondrous contemplation is like holding up a bright mirror and seeing one’s own face. Until the wondrous contemplation is accomplished and the surpassing realm shines clear, at that moment one feels that one has personally entered that realm: not leaving the Saha world, one’s body dwells in the Land of Bliss. It is what is called: that realm does not come and this body does not go; causes and conditions accord, and the facts appear plainly. If one can understand and cultivate in this way, it may also be called most sudden and most perfect; therefore it is likewise named the Buddha-recitation samadhi. What is called the true realm of quiescent light is the one-object three truths [the very body as the conventional, the true, and the middle]. Awakening to this true realm of quiescent light, one can well understand that one realm perfectly manifests all realms and one realm wholly gathers in all realms. Though realms differ in a thousand ways, their substance belongs to the one true. Belonging to the one true, they are wholly the same as the real mark, not two, not different. Understanding this meaning, holding the name and cultivating contemplation are both entirely acceptable; they are mutually fused and wholly accord. But in this matter, the keen find it easy to cultivate and the middling and dull find it hard. Why? Practitioners of the age of decline are shallow in faculties and slight in the power of wisdom. Not having awakened to the true realm of quiescent light, they cannot avoid clinging to fact and turning from principle, deluding the mind and seizing on objects, unable to make mind and realm one suchness. One must understand that practice is aroused in dependence on the nature and that the whole of practice lies in the nature, and only then is one fit to cultivate contemplation. It is what is called: outside the mind no realm, outside the realm no mind; mind and realm non-dual, substance and function one suchness. Whether evil or good, coarse or fine, all realm-appearances are manifested by one’s own mind-only and are originally not external. Otherwise, with the principle of mind unclear and one’s face set toward objects, not only will the wondrous contemplation fail, but one may even breed ailments. Therefore the ancients emphasized holding the name, knowing well that it saves effort and is easily accomplished; they did not exalt the cultivation of contemplation, greatly fearing that with much effort it would be hard to accomplish. You should know that the one method of holding the name is most stable and most fitting. It requires only utmost sincerity, not visualization. Thought after thought cause and fruit accord; mind after mind beings and Buddhas merge. When the work has long been familiar, without one’s noticing it becomes one piece. Whether shallow or deep, faith and vows are always first. With one mind one dedicates it to the West, and none fails to be received by the Buddha; all return together to the lotus land and together verify the supreme Buddha-fruit. If you keep sincerity thought after thought and recite the Buddha with a deep mind, you will constantly be sustained by the power of the Tathagata’s samadhi fruit-sea concentration, and the light of wisdom will shine through. It will cause the afflictions of the six dusts and the obscurations of the five aggregates of your immeasurable kalpas gradually to melt away, all transformed into the great treasury of light of the Tathagata’s fruit-sea, wholly penetrating, all becoming one color. Another day the surpassing realm of Ultimate Bliss will appear naturally within the treasury of the light of the Buddha’s fruit-sea. Even if one wished it not to appear, it could not fail to. Why? Because cause and fruit accord; because response and stimulus meet; because vow-powers join; because they mutually take each other in. It is like the bright moon in the sky, its light embracing the four continents: it responds to all who have the conditions, and there is no water in which it does not appear. You should know that our Buddha is likewise: though his reward body is in Ultimate Bliss, his response body appears universally in the ten directions. If one who recites the Buddha can, thought after thought, gather in the false and return to the true, and with a settled mind await the response, then at the end of life he will surely see the Buddha appear. Reborn thus, a thousand out of a thousand are reborn, a hundred out of a hundred. Compared with deliberate visualization, is this not all the more effortless? The visitor then bowed reverently and exclaimed: Excellent! Your disciple has received much instruction and gained no little benefit. Only today do I know that the one method of holding the name and reciting the Buddha is, in Shakyamuni Tathagata’s teaching for a whole age, the surpassing, special, expedient, universally delivering method. Truly it may be said: reaching the top and reaching the bottom, most sudden and most perfect. The three capacities universally gathered, the nine realms wholly received. The great see the great, the small see the small; the wise speak of wisdom, the foolish speak of folly; those of provisional capacity follow the provisional, those of real capacity follow the real; the shallow enter shallowly, the deep enter deeply. Though each differs from the others, every one is received as one body by Amitabha’s samadhi fruit-sea and by his compassionate vow-power. Truly this is no vain saying. From today your disciple will uphold it to the end of this life, and according to his strength urge others, to repay the Buddha’s grace and the grace of my Master’s instruction today. Having spoken, he bowed in thanks, joined his palms joyfully, and departed. So I took up my brush and recorded it, appending it after this treatise as a protection of the right and a rescue from bias, to supply what the treatise did not reach. May readers be pleased to give it their attention.
Appendix: A Record of the Auspicious Response of Relics Descending by the Lamp

Since I left home, I have heard that the Buddha's power is inconceivable, the Dharma's power is inconceivable, and the power of sentient beings' minds is inconceivable. These three inconceivable things — now I have seen them with my own eyes. And what was it that I saw? Last spring, not reckoning my own mediocrity and shallowness, in the intervals of reciting the Buddha I composed a treatise named the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World. When the draft was first finished, I entrusted it to the layman Hu Songnian to take to Shanghai for publication. But after he took it away, I again felt shame and regret. I reflected that the treatise-makers of old had all fully awakened and personally realized it; their meaning and reasoning, their words and phrases, were profound and broad, thorough and penetrating; and even then they first requested the blessing of the Three Jewels before setting forth the profound meaning, all of it reaching the marrow and revealing the subtle. Even so, when a treatise was complete they would set it aside for a year or half a year, or two or three years, before having it engraved and circulated. I am an ordinary being laden with karmic hindrances, shallow in knowledge, coarse in literary expression. The draft just completed had many shortcomings; how could I rashly bring it out to the world? Therefore I sent a letter instructing Master Desen to be careful not to publish it, and to wait until it was revised and perfected before printing. Up to recent days, I again carefully revised the original draft, dividing and marking its sections, and it grew all the more easy on the eyes; the cumbersome I deleted, the brief I supplemented. Finally I added a conclusion, entitled 'Protecting the Right and Rescuing the Biased,' for fear that people might doubt: 'the Buddha-name is only six characters; how can it be taken as a school?' Within the text I directly point out that a single phrase of the Buddha-name is the whole of the Buddha-fruit; it can be broad or brief, it can unfold or gather. Broad, it embraces the three repositories; brief, it all returns to the six characters. Unfolded, it pervades the ten directions; gathered, it is drawn back into a single thought. This is precisely what is called 'controlling the six senses, pure thought succeeding in continuity.' Realizing this meaning is like a fisherman spreading his net — what harm that ten thousand threads appear together, and in an instant are gathered by a single cord. The wonder of the Buddha-name is precisely here. Therefore I first offered the treatise before the Buddha, earnestly beseeching the Buddha's blessing and his condescending proof. And making a vow before the Buddha, let me now set out the text of the vow in a few words: 'Your disciple respectfully composed this humble treatise, to offer it widely to fellow practitioners in the ten directions. May I, from this retribution-body of the present life on to the future Buddha-body, thought after thought in continuity, without interruption, always make use of this Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World, to benefit widely all fellow practitioners in the ten directions, guiding them all together to return to the Land of Bliss, drawing near the King of Vows, forever enjoying the wondrous bliss.' When this vow was made, after a day or two — it was the night of the third day of the tenth month — I was transcribing the draft under the lamp, and just as I came to the point where the questions and answers of the final conclusion were ending, I felt that some ash had fallen from the lamp onto the paper. I brushed it away with my hand, and felt that it was hard and round. I picked it up with my fingers and pressed firmly, and still it would not break. Bringing it near the lamp and examining it closely, I saw that it was purple and luminous with radiance. Only then did I know — could it not be a relic? Thereupon I placed it in a porcelain cup and offered it before the Buddha. The next day at noon, when the sun was strong, I took it out and examined it with a hand mirror, and saw its brilliance radiant, round like a pearl. It was then shown to the whole temple, clergy and laity alike, each one looking; as reported, its size, color, and light were not all the same. Everyone sighed that it was a rare treasure. Even now it is still kept before the Buddha. But because its body is very small, it is not easy to preserve. Yet I reflected again: my treatise was about to be complete, offered before the Buddha, earnestly beseeching his proof. Now, on the paper following the treatise, I received a relic descending — could this not be the Buddha's way of indicating his proof? Therefore I took up the brush to record it, appending it after the treatise, to inform fellow practitioners, so that all who read this treatise will pay deep attention, and each and every one will arouse right faith.

Recorded by the monk Liaoran, who is fed on gruel and rice at Lingyan, in the Non-retreat Chamber of the Zhen Garden of the Sea of the Buddha's Spring, on the fifteenth day of the tenth month of the thirty-third year of the Republic of China.

Note: from the treatise the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi, the Jewel King That Emerges from the World on to the last of the various texts, in all twenty-three relics were obtained. In size, color, and light each was different; because three were lost, twenty remain at present. Let the clergy and laity who come and go request to view and bow before them, so as to nourish faith and vows, arouse the mind to practice, and together gain the supreme benefit.

Appendix: The Bodhisattva Jue Ming Miao Xing Reveals the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi

Someone asked: 'When reciting the Buddha's name one cannot attain single-mindedness; what expedient should one use?' The Bodhisattva said: 'You need only put a stop to thoughts and settle your mind, and recite slowly and steadily. Make the sound accord with the mind, and the mind follow the sound. Reciting for a long time, you will naturally attain the clarity and purity of all thoughts, the mind and its object both extinguished, and enter the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi. In daily practice you must recite much, from a thousand up to ten thousand, with the mind never interrupted; then the faculties are most easily matured. If you forcibly try to make it single, you will never attain it.'

Explanation: 'To put a stop to thoughts and settle the mind' is to let go a single thought, with all conditions utterly silent. Like a bubble merging into water, the true and the false are not two. Then lift up a single call of the Buddha-name and recite slowly and steadily, neither high nor low, neither urgent nor slow. Only make the sound and mind unite; then random thoughts are naturally clarified. Through long practice it becomes one piece, mind and object become one, and without being aware of it one enters the Buddha-Recitation Samadhi. It is like a kernel dwelling within the fruit, real and full, unmoving as thusness. Thought following thought without interruption, the faculties are most easily matured. If you forcibly try to make it single, you will never attain it. This passage is a simple, direct, profound, and ultimate instruction, which the wise and the foolish alike can practice. May all readers pay deep heartfelt attention and, in accordance with the Dharma, cultivate by perfume-drenching — the benefit is immeasurable.
Entering the Chamber of Fragrance and Light, Lower Collection
Record of Instructions from the Lingyan Single-Mind Buddha-Recitation Retreat
One Who Wishes to Enter the Fruit-Sea of Samadhi Should First Know Grace and Recompense Grace

All we who practice the Buddha-recitation, wishing to enter the fruit-sea of Amitabha Buddha's samadhi, should first know grace and recompense grace. If one can know grace and recompense grace, then while rightly reciting the Buddha one will at once feel close to Amitabha Buddha's samadhi fruit-sea. Whenever one recollects, it is immediately present. With a single thought present, one realizes that one's own body is originally within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, neither going out nor coming in, dwelling at ease in right samadhi.
