Naturally thought after thought accords with the Buddha's fruit-sea, mind after mind unites with it. When the accord reaches the utmost, it finally becomes one piece. When a single thought becomes one piece, unmoving as thusness, real and full, it fills the Dharma-realm. Why? Because being able to know grace and recompense grace, one feels that within the Buddha's samadhi sea one must see the Buddha in every thought [see the Dharmakaya of the Buddha], and draw near to the Buddha in every mind [draw near to the Dharmakaya of the Buddha]; if one wished to leave it, it would be utterly impossible. It is like a filial child in the world, who his whole life dares not stay far from his parents; even after his parents have died, he still remembers them thought after thought — all because of knowing grace and recompensing grace. Practitioners of the Buddha-recitation should likewise be so. If one does not know grace and recompense grace, though one recites the Buddha all day, one cannot but turn away from the Buddha and be separated from the Buddha. Why? Because being unable to know grace and recompense grace, one feels that Amitabha Buddha dwells in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, separated by a hundred thousand koti of lands, as if wholly unrelated to oneself. Though the mouth recites the Buddha, the mind is in fact reluctant; hence, while rightly reciting the Buddha, one's thoughts inevitably flow onward, and the mind inevitably wanders in distraction. One cannot dwell in the Buddha's samadhi right samadhi, nor accord with the Buddha's fruit-sea real mark. It is like an unfilial child, thought after thought keeping far from his parents, mind after mind going against his home village.

What is meant by knowing grace and recompensing grace? You should know that Amitabha Buddha, through countless kalpas, has been our heavenly compassionate father. We, through countless kalpas, have also been Amitabha Buddha's kinsfolk of one substance. Through the kalpas our life of wisdom has been joined, father and son mutually bound; it is not a chance reliance or a forced taking of refuge. Amitabha Buddha's grace and virtue toward us sentient beings surpass that of our own birth-parents by a hundred thousand million times. Even to the end of the future, with counting and with simile, one cannot exhaust it. Why? Because although our parents' grace and virtue toward us is great, in the end they can think of us for only one lifetime. But Amitabha Buddha is mindful of us sentient beings through endless kalpas without exhaustion. It is said: though sentient beings do not recite the Buddha, the Buddha is always mindful of sentient beings. Moreover, although parents are compassionate and educate us, pitying and protecting us, they can only hope that I become an accomplished person in the world. But Shakyamuni Tathagata's compassionate education and Amitabha Buddha's pitying protection directly hope that I will end birth and death, transcend the ordinary and enter the holy, even to Buddhahood, and only then rest. Moreover, parents can only gather me in their physical body and protect me by the power of the mind. The Buddha can gather me in his Dharmakaya and protect me by the power of his spiritual powers. And parents can only give birth to my physical body; the Buddha can give birth to my Dharmakaya.

What is meant by 'heavenly compassionate father' and 'kinsfolk of one substance'? Amitabha Buddha, in the past countless kalpas ago, when he aroused the great bodhi-mind, originally aroused it for us. When he abandoned the throne of the wheel-turning king, he abandoned it for us. When he went forth from home under the Buddha Lokêsvara-raja, he left home for us. At his first going forth he was named Dharmakara Bhikshu; pitying us and all beings in the ten directions, with compassionate eyes he regarded them equally, as if loving a single child. Originally he was of the same true awakened mind as us, without duality or difference. But because we have been deluded, we are unaware and unknowing. Therefore Dharmakara Bhikshu, within his true awakened real mind, at once arose in the unconditioned great compassion and set to work the great compassion of one substance, and before the Buddha Lokêsvara-raja established the forty-eight great vows — originally establishing them for us. Then, through kalpas as many as dust, he cultivated immeasurable pure and wondrous practices — originally cultivating them for us. He adorned the four kinds of Pure Land — originally adorning them for us. Until merit and wisdom were fulfilled and every vow perfectly accomplished, and only then did he realize right enlightenment in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss — originally realizing it for us. The great name of ten thousand virtues is called Amitabha. You should know that the Tathagata's great name was accomplished by the power of his vows in former lives. He extended this expedient to guide sentient beings, causing them to take the name as their point of entry, saving all beings universally and returning them together to the Land of Bliss. From this they advance in practice and together verify the Buddha-fruit. This grace, this virtue — heaven, earth, and parents could not express a ten-thousandth of it.

Now let me trace back its origin. In the past, Dharmakara Bhikshu, before he had aroused the resolve, was originally, like us, an ordinary being. Because after arousing the resolve he left home life life after life and cultivated age after age, he therefore attained Buddhahood early. The Amitabha Sutra says: It has now been ten kalpas since Amitabha Buddha attained Buddhahood. The Buddha is never for a single moment not mindful of us. But alas, from beginningless time we have always been deluded. Because of this, life after life we create karma, age after age we fall. Sometimes we are in hell, undergoing all kinds of intense suffering; sometimes in the realm of hungry ghosts, burning with the fire of hunger; sometimes among animals, supplying the mouths and bellies of people. Often, for many tens of thousands of kalpas, we do not hear the names of the Buddhas. Even if we leave the three evil paths, we may be among the asuras, angry, hateful, and fighting; or in the heaven realm, clinging to pleasures. Even if among humans, we may be born before or after a Buddha, or in border lands of lowly birth — solitary and poor, hungry and cold, distressed and afflicted, stupid and dull, deaf, dumb, blind, and mute, with the six faculties incomplete, sickly and short-lived. Even if we have abundant food and clothing and complete faculties, we may not believe in the Three Jewels and create much evil karma. Though we believe in the Three Jewels, we may not recognize right from wrong and additionally practice non-Buddhist paths. Though we do not believe what is wrong, we may be solely greedy for blessings. Even if we cultivate both merit and wisdom, we may not believe in the Pure Land. Though we believe in the Pure Land, we may half-believe and half-doubt. Or we believe but do not vow; or vow but do not practice; or practice but not single-mindedly. Though willing to practice single-mindedly, we may not encounter a good friend and so lack progress. All these various hindrances are because our conditions are incomplete; the pure karma is hard to accomplish, and birth and death are not ended. Therefore, through countless kalpas, we are always in the Saha world, transmigrating in the six paths, undergoing all kinds of suffering without rest. The Buddha in his compassion is mindful of us, but we are unaware and unknowing. Now that we have come to hear and know this, we should arouse great shame and remorse, weeping tears like rain, thirsting for our compassionate father, seeking to see him thought after thought, never forgetting him mind after mind. How do we seek to see him? How do we not forget? Now we have fortunately obtained a human body and are born in the central land; though we do not encounter the Buddha in person, we rely on meeting the clear texts of the teaching. We further are able to draw near a good friend, who reveals the Pure Land Dharma-gate — direct and steady, simple and easy to practice, not requiring many lifetimes, able to be settled in the present life.

As for 'meeting the clear texts of the teaching' — that is the Amitabha Sutra spoken by the Buddha. This sutra is concise in wording yet complete in principle and fact. The World-Honored One Shakyamuni, with a thoroughly compassionate heart, pitying us heavily-obstructed ordinary beings of the last age, who cannot by our own power awaken the mind and reach the origin, break off delusion and verify the truth, specially extended an expedient and, unasked, spoke it himself, disclosing it fully without concealing the slightest. First he spoke of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, the splendor of its dependent and proper retribution. Next he taught the arising of faith and the making of vows. Having faith and vows, one should arouse true practice — holding the great name of ten thousand virtues, hoping to attain single-mindedness. This single-mindedness is the original awakening that is the common source of sages and ordinary beings, the true mind co-substantial with beings and Buddhas. When Amitabha Buddha first aroused the bodhi-mind, it was this mind he aroused. When he established the forty-eight vows, each and every one was established in dependence on this mind. Then, in kalpas as many as dust, when he cultivated immeasurable wondrous practices, each and every one was cultivated in dependence on this mind. When he adorned the four kinds of Pure Land, each and every one was adorned in dependence on this mind. Until merit and wisdom were fulfilled and he perfectly verified the supreme samadhi fruit-sea — that too was the perfect verification of this mind. We, through countless kalpas, submerged and drifting, losing our way and falling, life after life — what we lost was this mind. Up to the present life, though we have gained a human body and a slight acquaintance with the Dharma, we still cannot awaken the mind and reach the origin, break off delusion and verify the truth, end birth and death, transcend the ordinary and enter the holy. Therefore we entirely rely on the great name of ten thousand virtues accomplished by Amitabha Buddha's vow-power in former lives, borrowed as our point of entry, drawn into the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, dwelling at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. We need only harbor utmost sincerity thought after thought, and call upon the Buddha's name. This can cause thought after thought to turn away from the dust and unite with awareness, to return from the false to the true — like a river entering the sea, gradually entering, gradually deepening. It is said: a single thought of utmost sincerity, then a single thought enters the Buddha's real mark; thought after thought of utmost sincerity, then thought after thought enters the Buddha's real mark. And a single thought not flowing, not wandering — then a single thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi; thought after thought not flowing, not wandering — then thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi. If one can use the mind thus thought after thought, and reflect and illuminate thus, treading solid ground step by step, then from here on, reciting the Buddha, every phrase is powerful, every character flows from the Tathagata's real-mark right samadhi. It is said: the real mark is the great name, the great name is the real mark. Long-cultivated and matured, it needs no forcing. Though there are deluded thoughts flowing, in one moment of awareness they return. Though there are habitual tendencies wandering, in one illumination they cease. According with the original source, unmoving as thusness, real and full, it fills the Dharma-realm. Having entered the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea, one constantly receives the Tathagata's Dharmakaya nurture, his compassionate mind's protection, his samadhi power's upholding, the real mark's fusion, the wisdom-light's shining through, and the power of wisdom's penetrating clarity. This causes our countless-kalpas defilements of the six objects and the hindrances of the five aggregates gradually to dissolve, all transforming into the Tathagata's fruit-sea great-light treasury, wholly transparent, becoming a single color. Even if in the present life we cannot cut off entirely the outflows of views and thought, or in part break through subtle ignorance and personally verify the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, we can still by this reduce our flowing, dwell in the Buddha's right samadhi, and personally draw near the real mark. Like one who perfumes himself with incense — his body bears the fragrance. With this merit, we direct it to the West and make the vow to be reborn. Until the Saha retribution is exhausted and the Western conditions are ripe, the sublime realm of Ultimate Bliss will naturally manifest within the Buddha's fruit-sea light treasury. Then surely the compassionate father Amitabha and the holy assembly will personally descend to guide us, and we will be reborn in the Land of Bliss. As it is said: father and son through the kalpas, seeing each other in a single morning — what consolation! Relying on the Buddha's spiritual power, in a mere snap of the fingers we arrive. Having arrived in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, we return together to the seven-jewel lotus pool. When the flower opens and we see the Buddha, hearing the Buddha's teaching we are awakened, drawing near to the unsurpassed compassionate father and the pure sea of the assembly. We study and practice all Dharma-gates, accomplishing the power of patient endurance in non-arising, endowed with the five eyes and the six supernatural powers, perfecting the three bodies and the four wisdoms. Without moving the subtle wonderful body, we manifest immeasurable countless transformation bodies, always carrying out the Tathagata's commission, guiding in the ten directions the deluded multitudes, bringing them all back to the Lotus Land, together verifying the fruit-sea bodhi. The above is what is meant by 'one who wishes to enter the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea should first know grace and recompense grace' — a brief account of it is thus.

You should know that Amitabha Buddha's grace and virtue toward us sentient beings are equal to the fruit-sea, inconceivable and immeasurable. All the grace and virtue in the world cannot compare with it. If we are in the Saha world amid the cycle of birth and death, then even if through the end of the future, life after life, we ground our bones to powder and shatter our bodies, it would be hard to recompense. Only if now, thought after thought with utmost sincerity, we enter the Buddha's real mark, and mind after mind without wandering dwell in the Buddha's right samadhi, and in all times hold the Buddha's name, making the thought of death imminent, awaiting the Buddha's coming to welcome us and our rebirth in the Land of Bliss — then above we perfect the Buddha-fruit and below we guide sentient beings, all returning together to the Land of Bliss, together verifying the Buddha-fruit. With this merit we recompense the Buddha's grace. If we can thus know grace and recompense grace, then when we recite the Buddha we naturally feel that the mind has somewhere to return and somewhere to rely upon. This too may be called 'now, thought after thought, seeing the Buddha [seeing the Dharmakaya of the Buddha], mind after mind drawing near the Buddha [drawing near the Dharmakaya of the Buddha].' Through this we can gradually turn the karmic consciousness, and not be turned by it. If it is thus now, it will also be thus at death. Hence the ancients said: the mind that is in samadhi at death is precisely the mind that is reborn in the Pure Land. Reborn thus, it is certain that a thousand will be reborn out of a thousand, a hundred out of a hundred. May all of us tread solid ground, be mindful thought after thought, and not neglect this.
The Pure Land Dharma-Gate, Ancient and Present, Same and Different

All we who practice the Buddha-recitation should investigate and verify whether the Pure Land Dharma-gate of the present time and that of ancient times are, in the end, the same or different. If we say they are different, then our Buddha-name, recited year after year from dawn to dusk, is still the six characters 'Namo Amitabha Buddha,' without the slightest difference from the Buddha-name of ancient times. If we say they are the same, then why is it that the ancients who went west were each particularly easy? If they did not go, then fine; but when they went, it shook heaven and moved the earth. Those of the highest grade, at death, were welcomed by the Buddha — heavenly music by the hundred and thousand, banners and canopies without number, white cranes soaring, and strange fragrance filling the room. Everyone could see it, everyone could hear it. When they wished to go, they went; and when they went, they needed no one to assist them. Dying seated or dying standing, they went off at their own will. Even down to ordinary practitioners, all could know the time of death in advance, bathe, change clothes, sit upright and recite the Buddha, see the Buddha come to welcome them [see the Buddha's physical body], and pass away peacefully. Reflecting on each of these, how admirable! Why is it that among people of the present time, seven out of ten have difficulty in being reborn? Even if they attain it, it is very strained and they must be assisted by others. Examining the auspicious signs at their death, many of the highest-grade rebirths of the present cannot match those of the middle and lower grades of ancient times; the middle and lower grades, needless to say. Looking through the records of the ancients' rebirths, free and liberated, there are not just a million — hard to enumerate. Let me now briefly cite a few, so that everyone may know and thereby believe it is true.

In the past there were two laymen who, in ordinary times, were friends in the Way, regarding each other as lotus companions for birth and death. They agreed that on the day of rebirth they would notify one another and the two would go together. Later, one of them left without announcing. The other, only the next day, heard his son say: 'My father yesterday, without illness, went west.' When the layman heard this, he at once said: 'This old fellow has gone without a word; I need only the effort of a moment to catch up with you.' Thereupon he bathed, changed clothes, sat upright, recited the Buddha, and passed away. There was also a venerable monk, even more extraordinary. When it was time to go, he said himself: 'I am returning to the West, and wish to take an attendant along; who is willing to go with me?' None answered. Beside him a child replied: 'I will go with the Master.' The monk said: 'Go and bid farewell to your mother.' Because his mother took it as a joke and thought nothing of it, she casually agreed. Unexpectedly the child returned to the temple, and at once sat upright, recited the Buddha, and passed away. The monk, patting his head, said: 'Little one, why have you gone ahead of me?' The monk also at once joined his palms, recited the Buddha, and departed. In the past, too, there was the layman Huaixi, who at death, without illness, announced: 'I am returning to the West.' His family said: 'Wait until we heat fragrant water for your bath.' He answered: 'I have long since bathed in fragrant water,' and, chatting and laughing, he departed. Observing these five people, at death they were wholly untroubled by karmic hindrances, liberated and free. There was also a monk reciting sutras who met a pheasant flying in from outside, wishing to peck at him. At once a spirit in golden armor appeared beside him, brandishing a staff and driving it away, saying: 'The great master is to be reborn in the West; how can you demand your life-debt from him?' From this one sees that those who truly obtain the benefit of the Buddha-recitation can have even the karma of fixed retribution averted — how much the more karma not fixed. Why is it that practitioners of the present time, at death, are mostly troubled by karmic hindrances, their minds unable to be in control, in extreme pain beyond description? We should investigate where the ancients' attainment lay, and where the present people's loss lies. If we do not investigate where their gain and loss lie, and make it manifest and clear, then those who do not understand will not be convinced, and will surely say: 'The Buddha has no response, the Dharma has no efficacy' — betraying the practitioners and making vain and useless toil, handed round from one to another, misleading people no little. In what follows I will clarify and distinguish, so that everyone may know: the ancients at death, without karmic bondage, liberated and free, were all because their ordinary-time practice was effective in power. Whether they practiced contemplation or held the name, they could all deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. Since they could deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi, then all the ordinary defiling, karmic-consciousness realms naturally and gradually dissolved, turning to emptiness and stillness, even to annihilation, without the least remainder. There was only the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, all-pervading in the ten directions, filling the Dharma-realm. Therefore many of the ancients entered this real-mark right samadhi, refining the wondrous contemplation. Like holding a bright mirror, they saw their own image. Until the wondrous contemplation was accomplished, they personally verified the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark. The sublime realm of Ultimate Bliss, within right samadhi, appeared whenever they wished to see it. Whenever they recollected, it was immediately present. With a single thought present, they at once felt their body in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the past, the Fourth Patriarch, Master Fazhao, cultivating contemplation on Mount Lu, in samadhi personally reached the Land of Ultimate Bliss. He saw beside the Buddha a monk with a soiled robe covering his head. The Buddha said: 'This is Chengyuan of Mount Heng.' Therefore the master, upon arising from samadhi, personally went to Mount Heng to study under him, and at first sight became a faithful disciple. Not only those who cultivate contemplation — those who hold the name, if they have already deeply entered the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwelt at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi, and further are willing to practice with effort, cutting off delusion and verifying personally, the sublime realm of the Pure Land may also be seen in the present life. It is like a man entering the sea and seeing the dragon palace — what doubt is there? The ancients at death were able to be liberated and free, to go when they wished without needing assistance, all because they had personally verified the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark. Even if they had not personally verified it, they must have deeply attained the power of the Tathagata's real-mark right samadhi. All the above is what the ancients attained.

Why is that which the people of today have lost? Of the practitioners of the present time, they only know the provisional and not the real. Even if they practice, they can only apply effort on the provisional level; they cannot gather the provisional back into the real and be the provisional and the real non-dual, provisional and real one suchness. Hence the benefit they obtain is shallow and slight. The karma-power of countless kalpas is strong. For example, a cup of water — how can it extinguish a cartload of firewood? Again, like bathing: if the water is little and the dirt is heavy, how can one be clean? If one wishes to be clean, one must sit with the whole body in the bath, washing for a long time, and only then can it all be removed without remainder. We who practice the Buddha-recitation are likewise. If we wish the karma of the three times through countless kalpas to be pure and the three hindrances to be eliminated, then when we recite the Buddha we must with our whole body enter into Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, gradually perfumed and soaked, washed for a long time, and only then can our karmic hindrances be exhausted without remainder. That which the people of today have lost is lost in the powerlessness of their ordinary practice. Why? Because when they recite the Buddha ordinarily, the false does not return to the true; and at death, right samadhi can by no means appear. Because ordinarily their false thoughts flow, the still water of samadhi is dried up, appearances are jumbled and confused, and right wisdom is benighted. Though they have pure conduct, it is scattered; they cannot gather it and return it to a single mind. Even if there is merit, in the end it is provisional and small; hence at death the benefit is also small. It is like a fish in water, which relies entirely on the power of the water to move freely. If it obtains full water, it enjoys full bliss. If it obtains a great portion of water, it enjoys a great portion of bliss. If it obtains a little water, it feels only suffering and no bliss. If it obtains no water at all, in a moment it cannot move, and its life is gone. We who practice the Buddha-recitation are likewise. If one can personally verify the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, it is like obtaining full water. If one can deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, it is like obtaining a great portion of water. If one only applies effort on the provisional level and cannot deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, it is like obtaining a little water. If one does not recite the Buddha at all, then one is wholly unconnected to the Tathagata's samadhi sea-water, and the life of wisdom is cut off.

From now on we who wish to enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi — there are two kinds. What are the two? One is awakening; only the keen faculty can accomplish it. The second is utmost sincerity; both the keen and the dull can accomplish it. What is awakening? The so-called Amitabha Buddha's samadhi fruit-sea is originally real and full, filling the Dharma-realm. In every place, without exception, it is all-pervasive. All things in the ten directions are all contained within it. We, through countless kalpas, have always been within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, vainly living and vainly dying, unaware and unknowing. Up to now, though the mouth recites the Buddha, the mind is in fact reluctant; still thought after thought flows, mind after mind wanders. We turn away from the Buddha and are separated from the Buddha. It is like an unfilial child, thought after thought keeping far from his parents, mind after mind going against his home village. We cannot dwell in the Buddha's samadhi right samadhi, nor accord with the Buddha's fruit-sea real mark. Now we should, thought after thought, turn about and reflect; mind after mind, awaken. How do we turn about and reflect? How do we awaken? Constantly contemplate that this present thought's five-aggregate body and mind of ours is originally within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, neither going out nor coming in, dwelling at ease in right samadhi. And when a single thought does not flow, then a single thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi; when thought after thought does not flow, then thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi. If it flows, gather it and cause it to return. Long-cultivated and matured, it needs no forcing. Naturally, thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi, and mind after mind accords with the Buddha's real mark. From here on, reciting the Buddha, every phrase is powerful, every character flows from the Tathagata's real-mark right samadhi. It is said: the real mark is the great name, the great name is the real mark. If one can recite the Buddha thus, this is called thought after thought according with the Buddha, mind after mind uniting with the Buddha.

What is utmost sincerity? It is: while we are rightly reciting the Buddha, we can only, thought after thought, harbor utmost sincerity in the mind, put down the whole body, die to the mind and tread solid ground, without recourse to thought, honestly reciting on. Naturally, thought after thought turns away from the dust and unites with awareness, returns from the false to the true. Like a river entering the sea, gradually entering, gradually deepening. It is said: a single thought of utmost sincerity, then a single thought enters the Buddha's fruit-sea; thought after thought of utmost sincerity, then thought after thought enters the Buddha's fruit-sea. Since one can enter the Buddha's fruit-sea thought after thought, then while reciting the Buddha one constantly receives the Tathagata's six benefits. What are the six? One, constantly receiving the Tathagata's Dharmakaya nurture, enabling the practitioner to be at peace thought after thought. Two, constantly receiving the Tathagata's compassionate mind's protection, enabling the practitioner not to retreat thought after thought. Three, constantly receiving the Tathagata's samadhi power's upholding, enabling the practitioner not to be scattered thought after thought. Four, constantly receiving the Tathagata's real-mark fusion, enabling the practitioner to be full thought after thought. Five, constantly receiving the Tathagata's wisdom-light shining through, enabling the practitioner to be without hindrance thought after thought. Six, constantly receiving the Tathagata's wisdom power's penetrating clarity, enabling the practitioner to be thoroughly clear thought after thought. If one is of the keen faculty and receives these six benefits, in the present life one can produce all kinds of wisdom and all kinds of eloquence; in all speech the true and the worldly fuse, principle and fact are without obstruction. From here on, every phrase of the Buddha-name flows from the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea.' It is said: 'the whole is a single thought, a single thought is the whole.' You should know that to recite the Buddha thus is true Buddha-recitation. And to rely on the Buddha's power thus is relying on it to the utmost.

Even if in the present life one cannot cut off entirely the various afflictions and personally verify the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea, one still obtains the perfuming atmosphere of the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea. Hence the Great Being Mahasthamaprapta says: 'Like one who perfumes himself with incense, his body bears the fragrance — this is called the adornment of fragrance and light.' With this merit, direct it to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and make the vow to be reborn. Not only does one not lose the right cause of rebirth; upon being reborn, one's grade is high. Though one cannot, like the ancients, have any special auspicious sign that people can see and hear, one can, as death draws near, know the time in advance; the body is free from the suffering of illness, the mind is not benighted; right mindfulness is clear and distinct, and one is moved by the Buddha's guidance. At the time of death one is at ease, as if entering samadhi. From this one ends birth and death and transcends the ordinary to enter the holy — this is already quite sufficient.

If we wish to obtain the aforementioned genuine benefit, we should be mindful with utmost sincerity thought after thought and awaken mind after mind. Put down the whole body, single-mindedly recite the Buddha. Push forward with all our strength, not giving rise to falling back. Like coming out of a pit of excrement, like hastening toward a jewel-place. You should know that the lotus pool is before us and the cauldron of boiling broth is behind us. Once one enters the lotus pool, wondrous bliss is complete. Once one enters the cauldron of boiling broth, the pain is endless. If one can push forward with all one's strength, one is called a great man who has emerged from the world. One morning the Buddha comes to guide, and in a snap of the fingers one is reborn in the Land of Bliss. From here on, gradually advancing in cultivation, until above one perfects the Buddha-fruit and below guides sentient beings. One may say that the Buddha's grace and the patriarchs' grace are both recompensed, and that oneself and others are equally saved.
The Pure Land Dharma-Gate: Nature and Practice Non-Dual

The Pure Land Dharma-gate should take the nature-virtue as substance and the practice-virtue as function. Why? The Buddha said: all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature. And he said: all sentient beings have the Tathagata's wisdom-virtue and marks, but because of deluded thinking and clinging they cannot realize it. If one is free from deluded thinking, then all-wisdom, natural wisdom, and unobstructed wisdom immediately appear. Judging from this, one sees that the natural nature-virtue of sentient beings is originally wholly the same as the Buddha's. That which is different is only the karma-power of sentient beings. It is said: the Buddha, through countless kalpas, cultivated in accordance with his nature — called 'the nature-good cultivating good.' Until the good karma was cultivated to the utmost, merit and wisdom were full, and he dwells at ease in the Pure Land, forever enjoying wondrous bliss. Sentient beings, through countless kalpas, cultivate against their nature — called 'the nature-evil cultivating evil.' Until the evil karma is cultivated to the utmost, the hindrance of sin is deep and heavy, and they sink in the Avici hell, forever undergoing intense suffering. Judging from this, the two words 'nature' and 'practice' are of the greatest importance. But because of a single initial thought, a hair's breadth of error leads to the loss of an entire kalpa. Rising to bliss or sinking to suffering — heaven and earth are far apart. In truth, viewed with right vision, the single word 'nature' is originally thorough from top to bottom, most sudden and most complete. From the Buddhas of the ten directions above to the beings of the nine realms below, all equally possess the one nature, bright and complete, without duality or difference. But the gain and loss within it all rest on whether one uses the mind well or not. For example, a room in which a hundred thousand lamps are lit: although the lamps differ, in the end the light is one; the whole is the same, without the slightest difference. It is said: the lights contain one another, the lamps gather one another; they accord in full, becoming a light treasury. Like the great sun, illuminating without exception. But if among them there is one person holding a lamp, not using the mind well, carelessly dashing about and lighting fires everywhere, seeking only pleasure and not minding the danger — that person will surely bring calamity, and the danger is unpredictable. At the least he damages his property; at worst he loses his life. From this one can deeply understand that the two words 'nature' and 'practice' are of great importance; it goes without saying. Therefore the Buddhas cultivate in accordance with their nature; when their bright practice is complete, they become wisdom-virtue and marks. Sentient beings cultivate against their nature; bound by greed and defilement, they become deluded thinking and clinging. You should know that Amitabha Buddha, in the past countless kalpas, from first arousing the resolve on to Buddhahood, was at each step in accordance with nature. It is said: arousing the bodhi-mind — it was in accordance with nature that he aroused it. Establishing the great vows — it was in accordance with nature that he established them. Practicing through the kalpas — it was in accordance with nature that he practiced. Adorning with the ten thousand virtues — it was in accordance with nature that he adorned. Perfecting the fruit-awareness — it was in accordance with nature that he perfected it. Saving all beings — it was in accordance with nature that he saved them. From beginning to end, even to the end of the future, there is not the slightest thing beyond his nature.

Yet since the Tathagata's causal ground was thus in the past, our causal ground today should also be thus. Though sage and ordinary occupy different stations, and beings and Buddhas travel different paths, how does the nature-virtue of sentient beings in the end differ from the Buddha's? If viewed with the Buddha's eye, from the Buddhas of the ten directions above to the beings of the nine realms below, none are not within the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-awareness nature, all alike entering samadhi. Why? Because space is not great; the nature-virtue is greatest. Judging from this, one can know that we, through countless kalpas up to now, have always been within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi fruit-awareness nature, and have never departed from it. In all our times, when we stir the mind and think, doing good or doing evil, all is within the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-awareness nature, and the Buddha knows and sees it all. But because from beginningless time we have always been deluded, unaware and unknowing, we do not see the Tathagata's fruit-awareness true nature and do not know the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. It is like a fish dwelling in water without knowing water, a bird flying in the sky without seeing the sky. Therefore Shakyamuni Tathagata, with a thoroughly compassionate heart, pitying us heavily-obstructed ordinary beings of the last age, who have no Buddha to be near: though there are the three-vehicle canons, we cannot practice them according to the Dharma. Even if we could practice them according to the Dharma, among ten thousand there is scarcely one who verifies personally. Even if one could verify personally, if one has not cut off delusion and karma completely, one still cannot transcend the three realms. Even if one cuts off delusion and karma completely and transcends the three realms, one has not fully verified the three non-retreat stages. If one wishes to reach bodhi directly, never falling back, this is not attainable. The World-Honored One, desiring to give free course to this compassionate intention, therefore of his own accord spoke the Amitabha Sutra. First he taught the arising of faith and the making of vows; next he taught the holding of the Buddha-name. For this Buddha-name was accomplished by the power of Amitabha Buddha's vows in former lives — the whole of his perfectly realized fruit-awareness is manifested in a single phrase of the great name. He universally causes us who recite the Buddha, as long as we harbor utmost sincerity thought after thought and call upon the Buddha's name, naturally to enter thought after thought into the Tathagata's perfect fruit-awareness and abide in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. It is said: a single thought of utmost sincerity, then a single thought enters the Buddha's fruit-awareness; thought after thought of utmost sincerity, then thought after thought enters the Buddha's fruit-awareness. And a single thought not flowing, then a single thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi; thought after thought not flowing, then thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi. Like a river entering the sea, gradually entering, gradually deepening. If there are deluded thoughts flowing, at once gather them and cause them to return. Long-cultivated and matured, it needs no forcing; naturally thought after thought accords with the Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness, mind after mind unites with it. Every phrase of the Buddha-name flows from the Tathagata's fruit-awareness right samadhi. Having entered the Tathagata's perfect fruit-awareness, from now on every practice is cultivating in dependence on nature, with all practice in nature.

It is said: if we arise faith thus, it is in accordance with nature that we believe. If we make vows thus, it is in accordance with nature that we vow. If we practice single-mindedly thus, it is in accordance with nature that we practice. If at death we are reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, it is in accordance with nature that we are reborn. When the flower opens and we see the Buddha in the West, it is in accordance with nature that we see. Hearing the Buddha teach and awakening to non-arising, it is in accordance with nature that we awaken. Until the Buddha-fruit is perfectly fulfilled, it is in accordance with nature that we are perfect. Saving sentient beings — it is in accordance with nature that we save them. From today onward, even to the end of the future, we are not the slightest bit beyond nature. Hence the ancients said: the present single mind is intrinsically endowed with the myriad dharmas and with wisdom-light; above, it equals the Buddha-mind; below, it is the same as all the sentient. You should know that Shakyamuni Tathagata teaches us who recite the Buddha that 'in seven days one attains single-mindedness,' which is the real and wondrous mind of Amitabha Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness. Entering this perfect fruit-awareness real and wondrous mind, fused for a long time, one naturally is not scattered. Furthermore, one comes to realize that within it there is no dharma not endowed, no dharma not fused. It is said: adorned with the ten thousand virtues, benefiting without end, intrinsically present. Pure and clear, with nothing attained, intrinsically empty. Empty and non-empty without obstruction, real and full, intrinsically the middle. The mind that can recite is the single mind of the three contemplations. The Buddha that is recited is the single realm of the three truths. If one takes the Buddha as the sole school, then the whole mind is immediately the Buddha. If one takes the mind as the sole school, then the whole Buddha is immediately the mind. If one takes the non-dual perfect fusion as the school, then mind and Buddha at once fuse. If one takes transcending emotion and seeing as the school, then mind and Buddha at once vanish. The substance of the nature-virtue alone is manifest, fully revealed. The whole is a single thought; a single thought is the whole. Substance and function are not two; substance and function are one suchness. This is precisely what is called 'adorned with the Buddha's adornment, self-adorned; upheld by the Buddha's upholding, self-upheld.'

If one can comprehend as above and cultivate by perfume-drenching without retreating, and with this merit direct it to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and make the vow to be reborn, then at the time of death Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly, within this perfect fruit-awareness real and wondrous mind, will naturally appear and personally descend to guide us, and we will be reborn in the Land of Bliss. When the flower opens and we see the Buddha, our grade is certainly high. Why? Because to be reborn thus is to be born in non-birth, and birth without birth. Though all day one is earnestly seeking rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, one constantly accords with the principle of non-arising. The above is what is meant by 'the Pure Land Dharma-gate, nature and practice non-dual' — a profound and wondrous, inconceivable principle. All those of every religion who do not believe in reciting the Buddha and seeking rebirth in the West have not deeply entered Amitabha Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness. If one has deeply entered Amitabha Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness, and knows that from today onward, even to the end of the future, benefiting oneself and others, profound and wondrous without end, until bodhi without ever falling back — then if someone wished to obstruct him, not allowing him to recite the Buddha and seek rebirth in the West, surely ten thousand oxen could not pull him back. May all who understand deeply ponder it.
The Pure Land Dharma-Gate Has Fact and Principle

The fact of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the fact that is principle; apart from principle there is no fact. The principle of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the principle that is fact; apart from fact there is no principle. If one comprehends its principle, then at once the One True alone is manifest, profound and wondrous beyond thought; even great wisdom rarely reaches its limit. If one investigates its fact, then at once the ten thousand virtues all appear, shallow and near, easy to attain; even the foolish and ordinary can enter its gate. But the fact of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is supremely special, different from all other gates. The principle of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is entirely the same as all other gates. Why? What is supremely special: from Amitabha Buddha's first establishing the vows and his practice in the causal ground, he is transcendent and utterly different from the Buddhas of the ten directions. Therefore his fruit-ground enjoyment, the magnificence and purity of his land, and his skill in saving beings are also supremely special, different from all other gates. And what is entirely the same: from Amitabha Buddha's final attainment of Buddhahood, with merit and wisdom both full, his realized fruit-awareness fuses the three truths, truth exhausted and delusion exhausted; he perfectly breaks through ignorance and perfectly verifies the Dharmakaya; filling and pure, encompassing the Dharma-realm, he is called the Dharma-realm Body of the Treasury, equal and without difference to what all the Buddhas of the ten directions have realized. Therefore the Pure Land Dharma-gate — all fact is principle, all principle is fact, fact and principle fuse, fact and principle are one suchness — is also entirely the same as all other gates. All the merit and wondrous practice, the fact and principle cultivation, of the Pure Land Dharma-gate flow from this Dharma-realm. It is said: every dharma flows from this Dharma-realm, and every dharma returns to this Dharma-realm. Now, in what follows, I will briefly set forth the meaning of the fact-and-principle, same-and-different, of the Pure Land Dharma-gate, so that all of you may know.

I humbly observe: the Buddhas of the ten directions all have Pure Lands, and all may be sought for rebirth. Yet among the four lands, only the upper three are wholly pure; the land where ordinary beings and sages dwell together is not pure. It may have hells, hungry ghosts, animals, women, the defective in faculties, the Two Vehicles, asuras, and the three disasters and eight difficulties, and other such reproaches. Only the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss has all four lands pure, utterly free of the names of such reproaches. All who are born in that land possess the thirty-two marks of a great man, pure and fragrant, golden and radiant. Though that land has all kinds of wondrous birds of varied hues, they are all transformations made by Amitabha Buddha, who wishes the sound of the Dharma to flow abroad; there are no animals in reality. Though it has hearers beyond number, they all possess the Mahayana faculties, and are not hearers of the Two Vehicles. Moreover, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions where ordinary beings and sages dwell together, birth is mostly from the womb; only in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss is birth wholly by transformation from a lotus. Moreover, in those Buddha-lands, though the upper three lands are pure, even ordinary beings of superior goodness cannot be born there — how much less foolish men and women, doers of the ten evils and the five heinous crimes, beasts and animals. That they should seek birth there — how could it be possible? Even if the sages of the Three Vehicles could be born there, they rely wholly on the power of their own precepts, concentration, and wisdom to cut off delusion and realize the truth, to partially break ignorance and partially realize the Dharmakaya; with their own merit they dedicate and vow, vowing birth in that land, and only then attain rebirth. We have never heard that they all have the Buddha’s power to rely on. Only the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss possesses the four lands and the nine grades. From the great Bodhisattvas above to the wicked and perverse ordinary beings below, even beasts and animals, all may seek birth in that land. If by their own power they can know the mind and reach the source, cut off delusion and realize the truth, partially break ignorance and partially realize the Dharmakaya, and with their own merit dedicate and vow, vowing birth in that land, then the land in which they are born is the more excellent and wondrous, and the grade they attain the more lofty. Yet even if one’s own power is wholly lacking, provided one has true faith and earnest vows and holds the Buddha’s name, or cultivates various merits according to one’s strength and dedicates them with all one’s heart, relying on the Buddha’s power to receive and guide one, one may still be reborn carrying one’s delusions. Further, all Dharma-gates belong to vertical transcendence; only this Pure Land Dharma-gate is especially of horizontal transcendence, relying on the Buddha’s welcoming guidance, and so attains rebirth. Having attained rebirth in the Land of Bliss, even one dwelling in the lowest grade, the lowest birth, forever enjoys wondrous bliss and dwells in non-retrogression in the same land, and from there advances in cultivation straight to the Buddha-fruit.

Again, the Buddhas of the ten directions, though they have virtuous epithets that all may recite, are not easily responded to. Even if we, in a moment of extremity, call upon them, we can only be freed from suffering for a time, and at best gradually rid ourselves of evil karma and gradually plant good roots. Only Amitabha Buddha’s holy name of ten thousand virtues was brought to perfection by the power of vows made in former lives, and by this skillful means he embraces all beings. If we are willing to hold the Buddha’s name earnestly and sincerely, even to the end of our lives without retreating, it can enable us in this very life to end birth and death, transcend the ordinary and enter the sage. From then on we always learn from the Buddha and quickly realize supreme bodhi. Therefore Shakyamuni Tathagata, with thorough compassion and truthful words from his golden mouth, especially taught us to hold the great name of ten thousand virtues, hoping we may attain single-mindedness. This single mind is precisely the real, wondrous mind of Amitabha Buddha’s perfect fruit-awareness. For this perfect fruit-awareness real wondrous mind is like a mani jewel: the one reality alone stands forth, the ten thousand virtues all appear. The three bodies are perfect, the four lands complete. Host and companions interpenetrate, self and other are non-dual. The dependent and the proper are fused, form and mind are one substance. The land is the body, the body is the land. Body and land are non-dual, real mark is one suchness. Amitabha Buddha makes the whole of his perfect fruit-awareness real wondrous mind appear within a single phrase of the great name. He enables all beings who wish to be born in Amitabha Buddha’s Land of Ultimate Bliss: they need only, thought after thought, keep sincerity in the mind and hold the Buddha’s name, and naturally they will gradually enter deep into the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-sea and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s real-mark right samadhi. Like water resting in water, they accord by nature. When the accord reaches its utmost, at last it becomes a piece. When one thought becomes a piece, being and Buddha merge. Having obtained the Buddha’s atmosphere, the wondrous fruit must appear. Just as it appears, one suddenly feels body and mind transparent within and without, the fruit-sea wholly manifest, true and perfectly fused, filling the Dharma-realm, pure and clear beyond thought or speech. This is what is meant by using the enlightenment of the Buddha’s fruit-ground to penetrate the mind of my cause-ground, and using the mind of my cause-ground to encompass the enlightenment of the Buddha’s fruit-ground. The cause manifests the fruit, cause and fruit are simultaneous, the very substance is non-dual, truly thus. Long and long matured, one naturally gains single mind. Having gained single mind, all inversion and scattering gradually vanish of themselves, and so it is called undisturbed. When such a person is about to die, Amitabha Buddha with all the sages suddenly appears before him within the perfect fruit-awareness real mind. He receives and guides the practitioner to rebirth in the Land of Bliss; by the Buddha’s spiritual power, in the snap of a finger he arrives. Having arrived in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, all return alike to the seven-jeweled lotus pond. When the flower opens and he sees the Buddha and hears the Buddha teach the Dharma, he suddenly understands. He then knows that the Saha world and the Land of Bliss, though separated by a hundred thousand million lands, are originally within his own present single thought of true bodhi mind, never going out or coming in, neither departing nor arriving. The whole fact is the principle, the whole principle is the fact. Fact and principle are perfectly fused, fact and principle are one suchness. Beyond emotion and view, inconceivable.

From this we can see that the Pure Land Dharma-gate is thorough above and below, most sudden and most perfect. In fact it is a great causal condition; in principle it is a secret treasury. It contains all Chan, doctrine, and Vinaya, and surpasses all Chan, doctrine, and Vinaya. Therefore the thousand sutras and ten thousand treatises point to it everywhere, and the sages and worthies of the past all turned toward it — as the stars revere the North, as all waters flow to the east. Yet there are students of doctrine and of Chan who will not carefully investigate and enter deep into the perfect principle of the Buddha-fruit, but rashly judge the Pure Land Dharma-gate to be Hinayana. Seeing others recite the Buddha and seek birth in the West, they scoff that such people abandon the root to chase the branches, seeking outward. Let them read this and ask themselves: what can they say then?
Opening the Buddha’s Knowledge and Vision, Entering It, and Dwelling in It

All we who practice the Buddha-recitation, wishing that at the end of life Amitabha Buddha’s perfect fruit-awareness may appear before us, that our own pure right mindfulness may be clear and distinct, and that we may move the Buddha to receive and guide us to the West in peace, must now have true faith and earnest vows, and thought after thought keep sincerity in the mind as we hold the Buddha’s name. If we are willing, thought after thought, to keep sincerity in the mind and hold the Buddha’s name, it can make us, thought after thought, turn our backs on the dust and unite with awakening, return from the false to the true; like a river entering the sea, gradually entering, gradually deepening. When contemplation and recitation are long matured, the hindrance of consciousness naturally opens, and we enter deep into the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s real-mark right samadhi. From then on, every phrase of the Buddha-name is clear and distinct. Suddenly we feel within and without transparent, the whole body fused, and we do not see the mark of change, nor the mark of flow, nor the mark of arising, nor the mark of ceasing. Know that at this time we are truly in accord with the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness, truly thus and unmoved. Hence it is called opening the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, entering the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, dwelling in the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Having already opened, entered, and dwelt in the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, one holds the Buddha’s name. From then on one constantly receives the Buddha’s power added to one and the Dharma’s power fusing with one, so that the afflictions of the six dusts and the coverings of the five aggregates from countless kalpas are gradually dissolved, all transformed into the great treasury of light of the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness, wholly transparent, altogether of one color. It is like black iron put into a furnace: in a moment it shares the color of the firelight. White ice cast into hot water: at once it is one body with the water. These are common worldly things, and they still have such power of fusion. How much more our Amitabha, the World-Honored One, who in former times on the cause-ground aroused great compassion, made great vows, and through countless kalpas long cultivated and long verified, adorned with ten thousand virtues, fused and unobstructed, perfect and pure, truly one suchness, inconceivable — the transcendent One-Vehicle bodhi fruit-awareness. If beings are willing, thought after thought, to keep sincerity and accord with it, to dwell mind after mind within it, and to hold the Buddha’s name, how could they fail to obtain the benefit of that fusion? Therefore Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta said: “If the minds of beings recollect the Buddha and recite the Buddha, then now and hereafter they will certainly see the Buddha and not be far from the Buddha.” This shows beings that recollecting and reciting the Buddha is the cause, and seeing the Buddha and becoming Buddha the fruit. He also said: “Without other skillful means, one naturally opens the mind.” This is what is meant by opening the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Again he said: “Like one who handles incense, whose body takes on the fragrance — this is called the adornment of fragrance and light.” This is what is meant by entering the Buddha’s knowledge and vision: borrowing the Tathagata’s merit and wisdom to adorn oneself. Again he said: “I, originally on the cause-ground, by the mind that recites the Buddha, entered the patience of non-arising.” This sums up the meaning above: I, originally on the cause-ground, by the mind that recites the Buddha, opened, entered, and dwelt in the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, recollected and recited the Buddha, and even partially broke ignorance and partially realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas. Know that the profound and wondrous purport shown by the Great One is naturally identical with the meaning above. It is all the Buddha-recitation Dharma-gate that the Great One himself practiced and personally verified on the cause-ground in former times. Now in the Saha world, out of great compassion, he reveals it to benefit beings. Hence the text goes on: “Now in this world I gather those who recite the Buddha and return them to the Pure Land.” This grace and virtue surpasses the chewing of food to feed an infant by more than a hundred thousand times. If we do not obey, and do not truly recite the Buddha and seek birth in the West so as to perfect the Buddha-fruit above and transform beings below, then even through the end of the future, though our bones be ground to powder and our bodies shattered, we cannot repay it. We should receive it with the whole body upon our heads and uphold it with one mind.

What is it to receive it with the whole body upon one’s head, and what is it to uphold it with one mind? It means this: since we can already enter deep into the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s real-mark right samadhi, from now on we may simply recite the Buddha with a focused mind. If we are willing to recite the Buddha with a focused mind, we constantly receive the fragrance of the Tathagata’s immeasurable merit and virtue and the light of his immeasurable wisdom, perfuming and shining through the whole body. This is precisely to adorn oneself with the Buddha’s adornment and to uphold oneself with the Buddha’s upholding. It is like a poor son who gains entry to the house of a wealthy elder: unawares, the Dharma-king’s treasury comes to him of itself, and he knows well that within it the hundred treasures are complete. Yet though the hundred treasures are complete, their very substance is empty; and though their very substance is empty, the hundred treasures are complete. Thus emptiness and existence are unobstructed, form and mind are one suchness. This is what is meant by the middle-way real mark, the ultimate truth. If we can, thought after thought, keep sincerity and accord with it, and dwell mind after mind within it, that is what is meant by receiving it with the whole body upon one’s head.

Further, this perfect fruit-awareness, if viewed from the cause-ground of beings, is merely called the single mind. Within the single mind the ten thousand dharmas are contained; the ten thousand dharmas, perfectly fused, are originally the single mind. This single mind is the vast, perfect, real-mark, unobstructed mind. Within it no dharma is not contained, no dharma is not fused. In the ordinary it is not diminished; in the sage it is not increased. It may become a being, it may become a Buddha; it may be cause, it may be fruit. On the side of beings, the whole of it belongs to the cause. Even one greatly and thoroughly awakened, with the whole perfectly manifest — where, after all, is the ultimate adornment? It can only be called the bare Dharmakaya. Therefore, from ancient times to now, many great good teachers versed in both Chan and doctrine, who had thoroughly awakened to the mind-source and greatly opened the perfect understanding, were yet willing to put down the whole body, tread solid ground step by step, and devote themselves to pure karma, contemplating, holding the name, bowing, reading and reciting, vowing and seeking rebirth in the Land of Bliss. This is precisely to borrow the Tathagata’s merit and wisdom to adorn one’s own original-awakening true mind. On the side of the Tathagata, the whole of it belongs to the fruit: originally the one reality alone stands forth, the ten thousand virtues all appear, the three bodies are perfect, the four lands complete, enjoyment is sovereign, benefit inexhaustible — and there is no need to cultivate further.

Therefore we now, with true faith and earnest vows, thought after thought keeping sincerity in the mind and holding the Buddha’s name, are precisely borrowing the fruit to gather in the cause and from the cause hastening to the fruit. It is also called borrowing the fruit to penetrate the cause and from the cause manifesting the fruit; also called cause and fruit mutually containing, being and Buddha merging with each other. Cause is fruit, cause and fruit are simultaneous; the very substance is non-dual, real mark is one suchness. This is what is meant by contemplating the body as real mark, and contemplating the Buddha and beings likewise. One who wishes to see Amitabha Tathagata’s suchness-Dharmakaya sees it at will by this means. All the above is the wondrous function, inherently possessed by the true mind, of sages and ordinary beings sharing one source and beings and Buddhas being one substance, together with the ripening, through kalpas, of the karmic conditions between Amitabha and beings. Now that we have met it, borrowing the fruit to perfect the cause is like water meeting water: an accord by nature. If we can, thought after thought, comprehend it and mind after mind accord with it, that is what is meant by upholding it with one mind.

There are those who do not understand, and doubt that this single mind, in which being and Buddha, cause and fruit, are one substance, belongs to the practitioner alone and has nothing to do with the Buddha. If it belonged to the practitioner alone and had nothing to do with the Buddha, then we might simply rely wholly on the Buddha’s power and merely hold the Buddha’s name; why would the World-Honored One have taught people to attain single-mindedness? For what is now called reciting the Buddha and seeking single-mindedness is precisely this: we now, thought after thought keeping sincerity in the mind and holding the Buddha’s name, thought after thought enter the Buddha’s fruit-awareness, even to the point that thought after thought we dwell in the Buddha’s Dharmakaya, relying on the Buddha’s nurture, receiving the Buddha’s added power, and being protected in the Buddha’s mindfulness. In the present we increase merit and wisdom thought after thought; at the end of life we move the Buddha to receive and guide us to rebirth in the Land of Bliss. Not only do we not lose the direct cause of rebirth — our grade at birth will be high.

Now we see many practitioners who, when single-mindedness is mentioned in ordinary talk, are somewhat frightened, and doubt and dare not enter. Even if they occasionally accord with it, they dare not plant their feet on solid ground and dwell in the Buddha’s right samadhi, fearing that to rely on their own power would betray the Buddha’s grace and prevent rebirth; they would rather cast it aside and rely on the Buddha’s power alone. To one with clear eyes this is like a dragon deprived of water — one cannot help but sigh. For broken gold that is not put into the furnace can hardly be melted; scattered thoughts that are not cast into the Buddha’s wisdom — how can they fuse? They do not know that the single mind is precisely the perfect fruit-awareness verified by the Tathagata, and that every phrase of the Buddha-name contains the single mind. Know that to contain the single mind is to contain the Buddha-fruit; hence it is called the cause encompassing the fruit-sea. Again, we now, thought after thought keeping sincerity in the mind, dwell in our own original awakening and hold the Buddha’s name. Know that to dwell in one’s own original awakening is to dwell in the Buddha’s fruit-awareness, constantly receiving the Buddha’s light shining through and the Buddha’s wisdom fusing with one; hence it is called the fruit penetrating to the source of the cause. It is not that apart from one’s own original awakening there is some other Tathagata fruit-awareness, nor that apart from the Buddha’s fruit-awareness there is some other original awakening of one’s own. Further, this Buddha-name may be taken as provisional or as real. The provisional person knows the provisional and leads the provisional back to the real; the real person sees the real, and the provisional is the real. What is it for the provisional person to know the provisional and lead the provisional back to the real? Before entering the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness, every phrase of the Buddha-name is only six characters, its measure no more than a sound; hence the whole real becomes provisional. What is it for the real person to see the real, the provisional being the real? After entering the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness, every phrase of the Buddha-name manifests the Buddha’s fruit-awareness, its measure equal to the Dharma-realm; hence the whole provisional is the real. So it may be said: the great name is the fruit-awareness, the fruit-awareness is the great name. Therefore, when the World-Honored One taught people to hold the great name of ten thousand virtues, hoping they would attain single-mindedness, his meaning was to lead them from the shallow to the deep, from the provisional back to the real, and thought after thought to accord with Amitabha Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness. Know that to accord with Amitabha Tathagata’s fruit-awareness is to accord with one’s own single mind; and to attain accord with one’s own single mind and become a piece, undisturbed, one must, thought after thought, keep sincerity in the mind and hold the Buddha’s name. Like water resting in water, like water joining water: long and long it becomes a piece, and naturally is undisturbed. Because the true and the false accord with each other and wisdom and consciousness are one suchness, it is called single-mindedness, undisturbed.

What is it for the true and the false to accord, and wisdom and consciousness to be one suchness? This single mind is originally the true mind of beings’ original awakening. But because we, since beginningless time, have always been deluded and do not understand how to return to the root and go back to the source, we therefore borrow the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness to return to our own original awakening. If we wish, thought after thought, to dwell at ease in our own original awakening, we need only, thought after thought, dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness. If we wish to adorn our own original awakening, we must borrow the Tathagata’s adorned fruit-awareness. If we wish to perfect our own original awakening, we must rely on the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness. What is ordinarily called the Buddha-recitation Dharma-gate — taking the fruit-ground awareness as the cause-ground mind, and the cause-ground mind as encompassing the fruit-ground awareness — means precisely this. Know that the cause-ground mind is one’s own original-awakening true mind. For although we, since beginningless time, have always been deluded, unaware and unknowing, in the end, now, this original-awakening true mind is equal in substance and measure to the Buddha’s fruit-awareness, lacking not the slightest. Therefore, if we can but, thought after thought, keep sincerity in the mind and hold the Buddha’s name, we naturally see gradually the pure light of the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness. Having seen the pure light of the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness, we see the pure light of our own original awakening. If we can add further diligence and perfume and cultivate according to the Dharma, we shall even gradually see the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness as vast and unobstructed, true and perfectly fused, with no inside and no outside, filling the Dharma-realm. Know that all of it accords with our own original awakening, one substance, appearing at the same time, responding to the same thought, with no before or after. Hence it is said: one thought in accord, one thought a Buddha; thought after thought in accord, thought after thought a Buddha. If one person is thus, each is likewise. For though the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness is perfect, everyone has a share in it and everyone may enter it. Only two kinds of practitioners enter it most easily and accord with it most easily.

What are the two? One is the highest keen faculty; the other is the lowest dull faculty. But the keen enter clearly, the dull enter darkly. What is the highest keen faculty? It is like the many clear-eyed people of old who were greatly and thoroughly awakened, in whose minds there was not the least doubt, who saw the Tathagata’s fruit-awareness as wholly fused, with no need to choose. Whenever they recollected it, it appeared at once. When a single thought appeared, they suddenly felt the body enter into it. This is what is meant by: without moving body or mind, enter deep into the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness; without leaving one’s own place, dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s real-mark right samadhi; accord with the common source of beings and Buddhas, truly thus and unmoved. It is just like the king of pearls in the pure ocean, pure and bright, reaching in all four directions, shining everywhere thought after thought. They felt of themselves that every phrase of the Buddha-name flowed out from the pearl-king, and again they felt that every phrase of the Buddha-name filled the pure ocean. Therefore Master Chewu said: Wholly clarifying all defilements, perfectly manifesting the original void, suddenly according with the spiritual source, going straight to the fruit-sea. This is what is meant by entering clearly. What is the lowest dull faculty? It is like the many simple, honest foolish men and women of today: though they cannot read a single character, cannot understand a single passage, and are not skilled at judging right and wrong, good and bad, yet when taught to give rise to faith, make vows, and recite the Buddha earnestly and sincerely, seeking birth in the West, they can bring forth the mind, believe and accept, and simply recite on without ever changing, without a single doubt, knowing only that the more the better. Instead they can recite until within and without accord and the faculties and dusts are one suchness, with only the Buddha-name clear and distinct, like a spring flowing in the ground, unbroken thought after thought. Hence it is called secretly penetrating the Buddha’s wisdom and darkly according with the wonder of the Way. This is what is meant by entering darkly. Because they benefit from reciting the Buddha, yet do not themselves know it. The ancients had a simile that expresses this very well: it is just like a poor woman who carries in her womb a wheel-turning sage king, yet knows nothing of it at all, and spends her days begging from place to place. Only the gods know that the child in her womb will certainly be a first-rate wheel-king, with the thirty-two marks, the eighty excellences, a thousand sons around him, the hundred treasures complete, all people relying on him, his benefit inexhaustible. This shows that foolish people who recite the Buddha often gain many benefits while knowing nothing of it — it is just the same.

They often say: “I am afflicted; I cannot read, do not understand the sutras’ meaning, and do not know how to cultivate.” Only the Buddha knows that in the future, when this person’s life ends, he will certainly be reborn in the West, transformed from a lotus, and in the end become a Buddha, universally saving beings. Because he obtains the true benefit of Buddha-recitation, before his life ends he can foreknow the time of his coming. He bathes, changes clothes, sits upright and recites the Buddha. His body has no sickness, his mind is not confused. He sees the Buddha come to welcome him and passes peacefully to the West. All this comes from being perfumed and shone upon by the fragrance and light of the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness, and from the added power and reception of the Buddha’s compassionate vows; hence at death the Buddha comes to receive and guide him, and he is reborn in the West at ease. Besides these two kinds of practitioners, there is one more kind that enters most easily and accords most easily. What is this one kind? It is children who recite the Buddha — it comes from their nature, with no need for forcing. Because their disposition is simple and good, their greed and attachment are light, their scattered thoughts are very few, and the karma they create is also little. When they are willing to recite the Buddha and cultivate, everything they do comes from what is true, with not the least pretense or ornament. Therefore quite often some children, at the end of life, are reborn with excellent auspicious signs. Many adults who have recited the Buddha for decades cannot match the benefit these children obtain. All this is because in ordinary times their recitation is unmixed, and so they naturally accord with the Buddha’s fruit-awareness: cause and fruit contain each other, vow-power meets vow-power, response and spiritual communion intertwine, like a magnet drawing iron. Though their ordinary effort is very small, the benefit at death is powerful — and great beyond measure.

Apart from these three kinds, the rest of us ordinary practitioners of the Buddha-recitation, if we wish to obtain the true benefit of Buddha-recitation, must all force ourselves to make good use of methods and antidotes — and why is this harder than for others? Because of the various discriminations of right and wrong that we have read in books and heard with our ears in ordinary times, which we cannot forget; and because of the various perfumings of greed and defilement with the dusts of affliction, which we cannot put to rest. It is as they say: if discrimination is not forgotten, the two extremes are hard to decide; if the perfuming does not cease, the road ahead is blocked. We wish mind and Buddha to be one suchness, but it insists on mixing in between. Add to this that most people always have some desire for fame and profit and some concern for face, calculating and scheming at every moment, which is also hard to wipe out. Even if one can cultivate diligently, by reckoning it is more empty than real. In the end one cannot match the foolish and the children, who act from nature, pure and unmixed, advancing thought after thought, treading solid ground step by step, dwelling at ease in the single mind, reciting the Buddha with single devotion — gaining the great advantage and full enjoyment. Therefore this late student has often said: to obtain the true benefit of Buddha-recitation, we must learn from the foolish men and women — do not raise doubt, do not give rise to discrimination. We need only keep sincerity and hold the Buddha’s name, like a hen brooding on her eggs, like a dragon guarding its pearl: not letting go thought after thought, not forgetting mind after mind. If we feel deluded thoughts flowing past, at once gather them and make them return. Long and long matured in contemplation and recitation, we naturally and gradually accord with the Tathagata’s perfect fruit-awareness and dwell at ease in the Tathagata’s real-mark right samadhi. It may be called arranging without arranging, and it is what is meant by not expecting it, yet so it is. If you do not believe it, then test it now: only a moment’s effort is needed to know that this method is most wonderful. It is like a bee gathering honey — once it tastes the honey, you cannot drive it away, and when chased off it comes back. Again, like a child eating sugar: the more he eats, the more he wants. When the recitation reaches this, one may be said to have tasted a little of the flavor. If one is willing to add further diligence, perfuming and cultivating long without retreat, one can surely open, enter, and dwell in the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Even if one cannot enter clearly, one will certainly enter darkly. And having entered darkly, pure karma can be accomplished and rebirth in the West may be hoped for. Having attained rebirth in the West, from then on birth and death can be ended, the Buddha-way accomplished, beings saved — and that is enough. Those with aspiration, please take deep note.
Self-Power and Other-Power Must Be Attended to Together, Neither Neglected

I humbly observe: the Buddha’s power is inconceivable, the Dharma’s power is inconceivable, and the mind-power of beings is also inconceivable. These three inconceivables are called the accord of faculty and teaching and the union of mind and nature — like space according with space, like water joining water. When the accord reaches its utmost, at last it becomes a piece. When one thought becomes a piece, self and other are one suchness. Knowing this and cultivating thus, the easier it is for effort to bring results, and the faster the work of the Way is accomplished. Since there is such an inconceivable power of mutual completion, we should attend to them together and neglect none. Otherwise, holding to one and discarding another, the practitioner, even with cultivation, can only perfume and form seeds as distant causes for later lives, and in the present life can hardly gain real benefit. What is holding to one and discarding another? It is either to believe in self-power alone and not in other-power, or to believe in other-power alone and not in self-power, or to believe in both and yet make no effort at all in cultivation. Wherever anything is lacking, it cannot be called the power of the three inconceivables completing one another.

What is it to attend to self-power and other-power together? The inconceivable mind-power of beings is self-power; the inconceivable Buddha-power and Dharma-power is other-power. Again, the one who cultivates is self-power, and the Dharma cultivated is other-power.
